       a)   BYLAW NO. 1777
            "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 534 (2670 Peatt Rd and 813 Arncote Ave),
            2018".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1777 at 5:33 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Parsi Developments Ltd has applied on behalf of Xian
Ventures Ltd to amend the zoning of 2670 Peatt Rd and 813 Arncote Ave from the R2 (One- and Two-Family
Residential) Zone to the MU1A (Mixed Use Residential Commercial) Zone.

                                                                                                          December 3rd, 2018
                                                                                                                Page 2 of 15


      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately a 21 unit multi-family
      residential building. As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
      regulations of the Local Government Act.

      In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

     a)    That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
           dwelling unit, prior to the issuance of a Building Permit:

           i.    $2,562 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                 $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

     b) That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:
         i.  A technical memo from a qualified engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately managed
             on-site for the proposed development, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
        ii.  A traffic impact study from a qualified professional that this development will have on the
             surrounding road network, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.
       iii.  Frontage drawings that indicate whether or not road dedication is needed.

     c)    That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all
           other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

           i.    That a stormwater management and maintenance plan be created, to the satisfaction of the
                 Director of Engineering, and registered on title for the benefit of future owners;
           ii.   That full frontage improvements be completed as per the Subdivision and Development Servicing
                 Bylaw No. 1000 standards, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to the issuance
                 of a Building Permit;
          iii.   That all recommended improvements stemming from the completed traffic impact study be
                 completed prior to issuance of a building permit.
          iv.    That appropriate corner cuts are provided to the satisfaction of the Manager of Land Development
                 prior to the issuance of a building permit;
          v.     That no unit created may have more than two bedrooms; and
          vi.    That the onsite visitor parking be painted as 'Visitor' parking and that these spaces be designated
                 as common property, not limited common property, on the strata plan.

1.   Authorize the Director of Planning to issue the following variances within the Development Permit for 2670
     Peatt Road and 813 Arncote Avenue:

      a) That Section 6.51A.07(1)(a) be varied to reduce the minimum front yard setback from 2.0m to 1.3m;
         and
      b) That Section 6.41A.07(1)(b) be varied to reduce the minimum exterior side yard setback from 2.0m to
         1.4m, and
      c) That Section 6.51A.07(1)(c) be varied to reduce the minimum rear yard setback from 7.5m to 4.6m

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation. Notifications and
      advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

                                                                                                 December 3rd, 2018
                                                                                                       Page 3 of 15

        b)   BYLAW NO. 1809
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 549, (MUE1 Amendments — 2750 Leigh Rd),
             2018".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1809 at 5:39 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Les Bjola of Turner Lane Development Corporation has
applied on behalf of 1096234 BC Ltd./Langford Ridge Limited Partnership to make various amendments to
the MUE1 (Mixed Used Employment 1) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to include underground vehicle storage, underground mini-storage as
permitted uses; replace hospital with health centre to allow for greater range of health services, etc. As
part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

•   $1,000,000 towards the City's General Amenity Reserve Fund; OR
•   An alternate amenity with a demonstrable value equivalent to $1,000,000; OR
•   A transfer of 15% of the lands located within the Mixed-Use Employment 1 (MUE1) Zone to the City of
    Langford; OR
•   Some equivalent combination of a(1) and /or a(ii) and/or a(iii).
•   As previously mentioned, the applicant is required to complete frontage improvements and off-site
    improvements as per the recommendations in the Traffic Impact Study and Bylaw 1507. All
    improvements are to be at the developers' expense; therefore, the direct capital costs to the
    municipality will be negligible.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Mixed Use Employment Centre designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

Resident on Donna Avenue— Is concerned about traffic on Donna and Hartsdale Road and about vacant
homes with homeless in the vicinity. Resident is also concerned about the speed of traffic trucks.

                                                                                                  December 3rd, 2018
                                                                                                        Page 4 of 15




Resident on Sergio Place (provided a five (5) slide PowerPoint presentation) — Is concerned about pedestrian
access around his house and being surrounded by development. The neighbourhood has been destroyed.
He requests that we deny access of Sergio Place to pedestrians, make purchases of homes as per original
assembly and that we stop site prep until loss of enjoyment is prevented.

Resident on Hartsdale Drive — Wanted confirmation that nothing will happen until proper access is put in
off of Leigh Road.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

Resident on Lake End Road —Addressed Council stating that residents have been patient with land clearing,
development, traffic increases and difficulty to turn left onto Leigh Road from Goldstream Avenue.
Sidewalks on Leigh Road are not finished, there are no crosswalks. People have to walk into traffic on Leigh
Road. Resident is concerned with overdevelopment. Despite development, the concern balance is slipping.
Notice of rezoning was placed in obscure location. Meeting time is difficult, there is no consultation and the
pace of development is too fast.

Resident on Goldstream Avenue — Addressed Council concerned that there is no community involvement,
no oversite by Council and promises are broken regarding logging trucks.

Resident on Wagener Terrace — Asked when sewer will come to their street.

Resident on Leigh Road — Is concerned about erosion of community, speed of vehicles, traffic and widening
of Leigh Road to five (5) lanes.

Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the Public Hearing
for Bylaw No. 1809 closed at 6:24 pm.

The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1839 at 5:32 pm, and read a statement to inform
those present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Matthew McKay of DB Services has applied on behalf of
1082116 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 801 Goldstream Ave; 2816, 2822, 2826, 2832, 2834, 2838 & 2844
Peatt Rd; 816 & 818 Hockley Ave from the C3 (District Commercial) and R1 (One-Family Residential) to MU2
(Mixed-Use Residential Commercial 2) Zone.


This is being proposed in order to allow a future multi-storey commercial and residential development.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.


Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.


The Acting Mayor called a first time for presentations.

     •   Resident on Rowils Crescent spoke in support of increasing density in the City core, and asked
         questions regarding wood construction, a new location for the displaced business, and whether the
         City would consider reducing parking requirements to encourage alternative transportation
     •   Business Owner on Goldstream Avenue requested information about business access during
         construction
     •   Business Representative on Peatt Road expressed concern that parking access be maintained during
         construction
     •   Resident on Goldstream Avenue shared concerns about pedestrian safety at the proposed
         roundabout at Peatt and Hockley
     •   Resident on Goldstream Avenue spoke regarding vibrations, increased traffic and limited parking
         during construction
     •   Resident on Goldstream Avenue expressed concern about the proposed height of the building
     •   Resident on Hockley Avenue estimated that construction could last 4.5- 6 years, and raised concerns
         about the associated impact on traffic, parking, and neighbourhood businesses
     •   Resident on Peatt Road echoed concerns about lengthy construction period required and proposed
         building height
     •   Resident on Hockley Avenue raised concerns about the increased traffic once the building(s) are
         built, and safety of nearby intersections

                                                                                                        July 15th, 2019
                                                                                                          Page 3 of 11


     •   Resident on Goldstream Avenue expressed support for wood construction, DB Services, and the
         increased densification and height of buildings as long as concerns are addressed
     •   Resident on Hockley Avenue expressed a desire to see the plan for buildout of the site before the
         project is approved
     •   Matthew McKay of DB Services provided the following information:
              o   Timber construction is innovative and speeds construction
              o   Parking will be created onsite
              o   The traffic impact is expected to be negligible
              o   Existing storefronts will be accessible during construction
              o   Construction noise will be mitigated where possible
              o   DB Services will work with Langford Engineering on road closures
     •   A resident requested information about visibility at the proposed roundabout for pedestrians
     •   Business Owner on Peatt Road requested clarification on the location of the proposed roundabout
     •   Director of Engineering Michelle Mahovlich confirmed that roundabouts will be installed both at
         the intersections of Peatt and Hockley, and Goldstream and Peatt
     •   A resident requested further information about the number of units per tower, expected number
         of residents, planned number of parking spots, and the traffic study
     •   A resident stated that a roundabout is not an effective solution to existing traffic issues
     •   Resident on     Rowils Crescent stated that       reducing parking encourages other modes of
         transportation, and that roundabouts increase safety
     •   Business Owner on Goldstream Avenue requested confirmation that business access will be
         maintained during construction

canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
That Council:


Direct Staff to prepare a bylaw to amend the Official Community Plan designation of 1000 Citation Road and
2691 Secretariat Way from Neighbourhood to Mixed Use Employment Centre;


Direct Staff to prepare a bylaw to amend the zoning designation of the property located at 1000 Citation
Road from R2 (One-and Two-Family Residential) to RM2A (Attached Housing) and the property located at
2691 Secretariat Way from R2 (One-and Two-Family Residential) to RM7A (Medium Density Apartment)
subject to the following terms and conditions:


    a)   That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
         residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:

              i. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund; and

             ii. $3,660 towards the General Amenity Fund.

         The apartment component may be subject to reductions depending on the use and height in
         accordance with the Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.


    b) That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:

              i. A technical memo from an engineer that verifies stormwater can be adequately managed
                     on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

             ii. Conceptual design drawings for both 1000 Citation Road and 2691 Secretariat Way to the
                     satisfaction of the Director of Planning.


    c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority
         of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

              i. That all frontage improvements to Bylaw No. 1000 standards are provided to the
                     satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a building permit
                     including any required measures from the approved Traffic Impact Study;

             ii. Complete remaining sidewalk on Citation Road to Florence Lake Road to the satisfaction of
                     the Director of Engineering;

             iii. That a Stormwater Management Plan be provided and all required measures recommended
                  be implemented to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a
                     building permit;

                                                                                                           July 15th, 2019
                                                                                                             Page 6 of 11


             iv. That a Construction Parking Management Plan be provided to the satisfaction of the
                 Director of Engineering prior to any alteration of the land;

               v.    That the required parking stalls for this development are allocated for the use by individuals
                     in each unit, as required by Bylaw 300 and designed accordingly, and that parking stalls are
                         not rented out individually;

             vi. That the 6 m portion that will remain road will be improved to the satisfaction of the Fire
                 Chief if the applicant proceeds with purchasing a portion of the road right-of-way.


Direct Staff to amend Schedule "AI" within Zoning Bylaw No. 300 to include 2691 Secretariat Way;


Direct Staff to amend the RM7A zone to allow for a height limit of 7 storeys at 2691 Secretariat Way;

Authorize the Director of Planning to issue the following variances through a Development Permit
application:

    d)   A variance to Section 6.31A.06(1) to decrease the front lot line setback from the required 5.5 m to
         3.8 m for townhomes located at 1000 Citation Road;

    e)   A variance to Section 6.36A.06(1) to decrease the front lot line along Secretariat Way from the
         required 7.5 m to 0 m for the development located at 2691 Secretariat Way;

    f)   A variance to Section 6.36A.06(3) to decrease the exterior side lot line along McCallum Road from
         the required 7.5 m to 2 m for the development located at 2691 Secretariat Way;

    g)   A variance to Section 6.36A.06(3) to decrease the exterior side lot line along Citation Road to 0 m
         for the development located at 2691 Secretariat Way.

             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 522, (804 Latoria Rd and 950
             Worrall Dr), Bylaw No. 1760, 2019".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1760 at 5:30 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Adam Weir, of Langdon Weir Construction Ltd. has
applied on behalf of Ridley Bros. Development Ltd. to amend the zoning of the property at 804 Latoria Road
and 950 Worrall Drive from the RR2 (Rural Residential 2) Zone to the RS4, Residential Small Lot 4, Zone and
to add to that zone the following uses for this property only:

                                                                                                   November 25^^ 2019
                                                                                                             Page 2 of 9


            o   Schools
            o   Group Day Cares
            o   Townhouses, not to exceed a total of 80 units;
            o   Small lot single family dwellings, not to exceed a total of 30 units;

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


It was Council's resolution that the applicant provide both a technical stormwater management assessment
and a traffic impact assessment with respect to subject property prior to this Public Hearing and to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering. These have been provided.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a bonus to the City for
increased density in accordance with Council Policy:

          $6000 per one family dwelling towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
          $3960 per small lot, one family dwelling towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
          $3660 per townhouse unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
          $1000 per one family dwelling towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
          $660 per small lot, one family dwelling towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
          $610 per townhouse unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

Prior to bylaw adoption, the applicant will provide a Section 219 Covenant registered in priority over all
other charges on title that ensures that:

    •   A stormwater management plan is provided and implemented to the satisfaction of the Director of
        Engineering prior to development;
    •   A frontage drawing for Latoria Road is provided to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering,
        and that any road dedication and all required frontage improvements in the Latoria Road corridor
        are provided prior to development and in accordance with the Latoria Road Master Plan and Bylaw
        1000;
    •   That temporary emergency access is provided for with each phase of subdivision, and that water
        flow necessary to comply with Fire Underwriters Survey requirements are provided with each
        proposed phase of development;
    •   That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or other
        servicing requirements are provided to Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the
        Director of Engineering and that costs incurred will be the sole responsibility of the applicant;
    •   That the applicant will construct full frontage improvements at their sole cost in accordance with
        Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering for all internal roads;
    •   That the applicant will implement the recommendations of the Traffic Impact Assessment, to the
        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
    •   That the applicant will provide a construction parking management plan to the satisfaction of the
        Director of Engineering prior to issuance of any building permit;

A separate Section 219 covenant is to be registered prior to any subdivision or alteration of the land, and
within this covenant the applicant will agree to provide a Development Concept Plan that secures the layout
of the development, and in particular identifies the following:

                                                                                                          November 25^ 2019
                                                                                                                    Page 3 of 9




    •   The amount and location of trail connections, dedicated open spaces and park spaces;
    •   The amount and location of streamside protection and enhancement areas in accordance with the
        Province's Riparian Areas Regulation and prepared by a Registered Professional Biologist;
    •   The amount and location of covenanted non-disturbance open space outside of the Stream
        Protection and Enhancement Area (SPEA);
    •   The location of the community and recreational amenities; and
    •   The location of the school site; as well as
    •   An estimate of the costs associated with constructing trails and installing park and trail
        infrastructure;

The applicant further agrees, by way of covenant, that there shall be no disturbance or structures within
any of the areas that are designated as non-disturbance areas and that a split-rail fence or stone wall will
be used to delineate these areas from development areas. In the event that any areas designated as non-
disturbance areas, outside of the SPEA, are inadvertently impacted during development the applicant has
agreed to remediate and replant these areas to a natural state in accordance with a planting plan prepared
by a registered professional biologist. SPEA areas will be protected and monitored on site by the project
biologist during construction and site preparation.

With respect to the Riparian areas on with the subject property, the applicant's proposal for dedicated open
space and covenanted open space encompasses all of the SPEA area required by the Province's Riparian
Areas regulation. The actual setback of buildings to the stream will be determined at a later date in the
Development Permit process.

The applicant will also, by way of a covenant, agree to include 10m2 of storage space, exclusive of closet
space, in any single family dwelling on a lot that is less than 400m2.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside or Shoreline designation, and in
particular meets Policy 3.11.1 with respect to the retention of public and/or private open space in Hillside
or Shoreline Areas.

        proposed phase of development;
    •   That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or other
        servicing requirements are provided to Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the
        Director of Engineering and that costs incurred will be the sole responsibility of the applicant;
    •   That the applicant will construct full frontage improvements at their sole cost in accordance with
        Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering for all internal roads;
    •   That the applicant will implement the recommendations of the Traffic Impact Assessment, to the
        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
    •   That the applicant will provide a construction parking management plan to the satisfaction of the
        Director of Engineering prior to issuance of any building permit;

A separate Section 219 covenant is to be registered prior to any subdivision or alteration of the land, and

canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
That Council:


     1.   Direct staff to prepare a bylaw to amend the zoning designation of the property located at 939
          Walfred from the RR5 (Rural Residential 5) to the RS3 (Residential Small Lot 3), and to amend the
          text within the RS3 zone for the subject property such that:


           a)        Secondary suites are permitted, in accordance with section 3.08, on all lots larger than 400 m 2
                     with a lot width greater than 12 m;
           b)        The total floor area of the of one family-dwelling on lots less than 400 m 2 may not exceed the
                     total area of the lots they occupy (e.g. 1.0 FSR);
           c)        The minimum lot size is reduced to 200


Subject to the following terms and conditions:


     2.   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus of increased density, the following contributions per
          new lot created, prior to subdivision approval:


                I.         $3,960 per lot towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
               II.         $660 per lot towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

                                                                                              February 4th, 2019
                                                                                                    Page 3 of 9


3.   That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:

        I.   A technical memo from a qualified engineer that verifies storm water can adequately
             managed on-site, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
       II.   A site plan that shows the 9.5 land dedication, and 2.0 m wide proposed statutory right of
             way that will link the subject development to Walfred Road;

4.   That the applicant provides, prior to bylaw Adoption, a section 219 covenant, registered in priority
     overall all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

        I.   That the applicant agrees that all one-family dwellings with a secondary suite must include
             a double car driveway, provided that the width of the driveway does not exceed 50% of the
             width of the lot.
       II.   That the applicant complete full frontage improvements, including but not limited to:
             bicycle laning, off street parking, sidewalks, light standards and boulevard planting, in
             accordance with Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the Director of
             Engineering, prior to subdivision approval;
      III.   That the applicant construct, or provide a bond for, a 1.8m high solid board fence along the
             rear of lots that abut the 7.0 m wide dedicated open space adjacent to Walfred Road, prior
             to subdivision approval;
      IV.    That the applicant provide a construction parking management plan, to the satisfaction of
             the Director of Engineering, prior to issuance of a building permit;
       V.    That no driveway or other vehicle access will be created between the subject property and
             Walfred Road;

      VI.    That the applicant dedicate a 2.5 m wide area of land to accommodate frontage
             requirements, and off street parking along Walfred Road, as well as an additional 7.0 m
             wide dedicated area of land to the City between Walfred Road and the subject property,
             prior to subdivision approval;
     VII.    That the applicant provide a stormwater management plan, to the satisfaction of the
             Director of Engineering and in accordance with Bylaw No. 1000, prior to subdivision
             approval;
     VIII.   That the applicant agrees to implement the approved storm water management plan and
             to complete any required improvements and/or upgrades to on site and off site
             infrastructure necessary to facilitate proper drainage on the subject property at the
             applicant's expense;
      IX.    That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions
             or other required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled at the applicant's expense;
       X.    That the applicant agrees to replant the 7.0 m wide dedicated area, to the satisfaction of
             the Director of Planning, contained within the tree retention plan for the adjacent property
             at 935 Walfred Road, prior to building permit issuance;
      XI.    That the applicant construct a 2.0 m wide pedestrian trail, linking the subject development
             to Walfred Road, prior to subdivision approval, which may be reduced to 1.0 m once the
             property to the west is developed;
     XII.    The applicant registers a statutory right of way for the construction of a pedestrian trail
             linking the proposed development to Walfred Road, prior to subdivision approval; and

                                                                                                          February 4th, 2019
                                                                                                                Page 4 of 9


        XIII.         The applicant registers a statutory right of way for a two-point turnaround, to the
                      satisfaction of the Fire Chief, registered in favour of the City, prior to subdivision approval;
        XIV.          The applicant registers a housing covenant for all lots less than 400 rn 2 that includes: a) no
                      more than two bathrooms and one two piece (powder room) permitted within each
                      dwelling, b) no more than one kitchen or food preparation area per dwelling, c) no separate
                      thermostat controls for separate parts of the single-family dwelling unit, and d) no
                      separation between floors or areas of the single-family dwelling unit.

means to the public. There are rumours that it is going to be turned into a golf club.

used as a recreation centre for twenty-five years. He further advised of the requirement to provide an
additional swimming pool.

pool can be placed.

The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No.'s 1461 and 1749 at 5:31 p.m.

The Acting Mayor advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that after
everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be
heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                       February 5th, 2018
                                                                                                            Page 2 of 10


     The City Planner advised that Niall Paltiel of Island View Strategies has applied on behalf of Seacliff
     Properties to amend the Official Community Plan designation of 790 McCallum Rd from Neighbourhood
     to Mixed Use Employment Centre and to amend the zoning of 790 McCallum Rd from the CH1 (Cluster
     Housing Residential) Zone to a new MUE2 (Mixed-Use Employment 2) Zone.

     This is being proposed in order to allow for a mixed use development, which may include medium to high
     density residential, commercial, institutional, recreational and/or assembly facilities.

     As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
     Government Act.

     In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

     a) That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contribution prior to
        issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval:

         i.   The dedication of 16,200m2 of land in a block form and location to the satisfaction of the Director
              of Planning; and
         ii. $1,000,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund for this site;
              OR
         iii. An amenity building on this site to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning, with a certified
              construction value of $1,000,000; and
         iv. $500,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund for this site;
              OR
         v. Arts and Cultural structure(s) on this site to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning with a
              certified construction value of $500,000.

     b) That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the following:

       i.     A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately managed on-
              site for the proposed development, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.
       ii.    The registration a 10m wide statutory right of way along the western and southern edges of the
              property for trail purposes; and
      iii.    Road dedication at Treanor Avenue for the future construction of a roundabout to the
              satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

c)    That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of
      all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

       i.     That a four-way signalized intersection be installed on McCallum Road at the main entry point to
              Costco (eastern side) prior to issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval;
       ii.    That a roundabout be constructed along the frontage of this property on Treanor Road prior to
              issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, to the satisfaction of the Director of
              Engineering.
      iii.    That a landscaped and irrigated trail be constructed along the southern and western edges
              within the 10m wide statutory right of way to bylaw 1000 standards prior to issuance of a
              building permit or subdivision approval, and to the satisfaction of the Manager of Parks;

                                                                                                      February 5th, 2018
                                                                                                            Page 3 of 10


       iv.   That all road dedication, including the widening of McCallum Road, and any new internal
             municipal road is provided prior to issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval to the
             satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and Approving Officer;
       v.    That a Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) be completed prior to issuance of a building permit or
             subdivision approval to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering for the proposed
             development, and that the recommendations of the TIA be implemented;
      vi.    That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are completed prior to issuance of a
             building permit or subdivision approval, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering; and
      vii.   That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building permit or
             subdivision approval and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director
             of Engineering.

d)    Direct staff to release the existing 30m wide restrictive covenant in exchange for Of a 10m wide statutory
      right of way for a buffer and trail.

               b)   That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:

                            Servicing Bylaw (Bylaw No. 1000) prior to subdivision approval or building permit
                            issuance, whichever is first;
                     iii.   That the developer agrees to implement the approved storm water
                            management plan and to complete any required improvements and/or
                            upgrades to on site and off site infrastructure necessary to facilitate proper
                            drainage on the subject property at the applicant's expense;

                            sidewalks and light standards, prior to the issuance of a building permit;

                            services to the subject properties are to be fulfilled at the developer's expense;

             & 2706 Sooke Rd), 2018".


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1767 at 5:31 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                   April 16th, 2018
                                                                                                       Page 2 of 8



The City Planner advised that Niall Paltiel of Keycorp Planning Ltd. has applied on behalf of Oakcrest Park
Estates to amend the zoning of 2668, 2674, 2682, 2684, 2686, 2696, 2702 & 2706 Sooke Rd from the C3
(District Commercial) and CS1 (Service Commercial) Zone to a new C9 (Community Town Centre
Pedestrian 9) Zone.


This is being proposed in order to allow a mixed-used development that may include high density
residential as well as commercial uses.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following contributions per
residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit, as a bonus for increased density:

      i. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund, and
      ii. $2,074 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund, for which Council may use this towards the
          construction of the realignment of Glen Lake Road and DCC works on Sooke Road.


The applicant has also agreed to provide a technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can
be adequately managed for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering,
prior to public hearing — which they have.

Additionally, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the applicant will provide a Section 219 covenant that agrees to the
following:

       i. That the owner will not apply for, nor is the City obligated to issue a Development Permit or
          Building Permit until road dedication is provided to the satisfaction of the Director of
          Engineering and Approving Officer.

       ii. That at any time after the 5 th anniversary date of adoption of the bylaw to rezone the subject
           lands, the City may request, and the owner shall provide, the area of land necessary for the
           construction of the road extension from Happy Valley Road to Glen Lake Road as well as Sooke
           Road for $1.00.

      iii. That the owner will limit direct vehicular access to Sooke Road, and will not apply for, nor will
           the City be obligated to grant driveway access on to Sooke Road, except in accordance with a
           comprehensive plan of development for the properties as a whole.

      iv. That a Traffic Impact Assessment be completed to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering
          for the full build-out of any block that commercial and/or residential uses are proposed on, prior
          to the issuance of building permit, and that the recommendations of the Traffic Impact
             Assessment be implemented prior to occupancy of any building;

       v. That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided to the satisfaction of the
          Director of Engineering and Manager of Parks prior to issuance of a building permit; and

      vi. That a detailed storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building permit
          and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

                                                                                                   April 16th, 2018
                                                                                                       Page 3 of 8



This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood and Neighbourhood Centre
designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.


The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Resident on Anders Road addressed Council wondering of there was an easement, as red ribbons showed
up 10 days ago.

Michelle Mahovlich, Director of Engineering provided a response.


Resident on Page Road expressed concern over height of the building and minimal size of setbacks. Also
wondered if change was because of inclusion of hotel lands.

Mathew Baldwin, Director of Planning provided a response and clarification.

Resident on Anders Road asked about density.


Mayor Young provided clarification (depends on stormwater and parking).

Resident asked about the realignment of Glen Lake road and about sound-deadening fencing.


Mayor Young provided clarification.

Resident on Anders Road is curious about setbacks and sound deadening fence.


Mathew Baldwin, Director of Planning provided clarification.

Resident on Anders Road asked about setbacks from the galloping goose trail.


Resident on Wilshire Drive asked about left hand turn from Sooke onto Wilshire.


Mayor Young and Michelle Mahovlich, Director of Engineering provided clarification and that traffic would
be directed through a signalized intersection.

Jim Hartshorne answered all questions.
    -   Ribbons — in realtion to a storm drain issue
    -   Fencing — 6 feet
    -   Density/Site coverage — less than the allowable 70%
    -  Sound deadening fence — definitely putting something idown Anders road
    -  Traffic — will improve Sooke Road in conjunction with Ministry of Transportation and
         Infrastructure and understood through traffic study


Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

None presented.

                                                                                                     April 16th, 2018
                                                                                                          Page 4 of 8




The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1767 closed at 5:52 p.m.

3.        PUBLIC HEARING

          a) Bylaw No. 1658
              "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 463, (1128 Finlayson Arm Rd), 2016".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1658 at 5:30 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Mary Rostad has applied to amend the zoning of 1128 Finlayson Arm Rd
from the RR4 (Rural Residential 4) Zone to a new RAE1 (Rural Agriculture and Eco-Tourism 1) Zone to
permit equestrian based therapy and riding activities on the property.

                                                                        Regular Council Minutes — October 17th, 2016
                                                                                                         Page 2 of 6



This is being proposed in order to permit equestrian based therapy and riding activities on the property.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

a)   A site servicing feasibility review must be conducted, to the satisfaction of the Director of
     Engineering, for any development prior to issuance of a development permit.

b)     That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority
       of all other charges on title that agrees to the following:
     i. That any necessary underground or above ground servicing upgrades, extensions, or other
         requirements should be fulfilled at the applicant's expense.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside or Shoreline designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Mary Rostad, 1128 Finlayson Arm Road - addressed Council thanking them for their support.

Tony James of Finlayson Arm Road — addressed Council in support of the proposed application.


Eric Stade of 1124 Finlayson Arm Road — addressed Council in support of the proposed application.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.


The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1658 closed at 5:35 p.m.

             1883, 2020".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1883 at 5:34 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Danny Jadresko, has applied on behalf of Woodsmere
Holdings Corporation to amend the zoning of 2627 Sooke Road from the R2 (One- and Two-Family
Residential) Zone to the C9 (Community Town Centre Pedestrian 9) Zone.

                                                                                                          November 2, 2020
                                                                                                                Page 2 of 26


This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 90-units and a single ground
level commercial unit that faces Sooke Road.

A public hearing was previously held on June 29, 2020 and Council passed the following resolution, 'That
Council direct staff to work with the Province and the 2627 Sooke Road developer to have traffic come and
go via Sooke Road rather than quieter residential streets.' The developer has since revised the site plan,
which now demonstrates residential traffic to and from the site will be from Sooke Road only.

At this time, Council may also wish to require the applicant to strata title the building prior to occupancy
and to include infrastructure to support electric vehicle charging.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

a)    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per residential
      unit, subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the Affordable Housing
      and Amenity Contribution Policy, prior to issuance of a building permit:

          i.     $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund; and
                 $2,074 toward the General Amenity Fund.

b) That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:

                 A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately managed on-site
                 for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

c)    That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a section 219 covenant, registered in priority of
      all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

          i.     That all frontage improvements along Sooke Road are provided as per the Sooke Road Corridor
                 Concept Plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and the Ministry of Transportation
                 and Infrastructure, and that any road dedication required to contain these frontage
                 improvements within the road right of way is provided prior to the issuance of a Building Permit;
          ii.    That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building permit and
                 implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
      iii.       That a construction parking and traffic management plan be provide prior to the issuance of a
                 building permit, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
      iv.        That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the proposed
                 residential building that ensures parking is assigned and tied to each unit created in accordance
                 with the minimum required parking stalls as per the zoning bylaw.

And finally, that Council authorizes the Director of Planning to issue the following variance in the Form and
Character Development Permit for 2627 Sooke Road:

     i.         That Table 1 of Section 4.01.01 be varied to reduce the minimum parking requirement from the
                required 2.75 spaces per dwelling unit with two bedrooms or less and 3.75 spaces per dwelling unit
                with more than two bedrooms to 1.25 spaces per dwelling unit with two bedrooms or less and 2.75
                spaces per dwelling unit with more than two bedrooms.

                    "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 590, (494 Goldstream Ave), Bylaw No.
                    1905, 2020".


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1905 at 5:35 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that WA Architects has applied on behalf of Le Gers
Properties Inc. to amend the zoning of 494 Goldstream Avenue from the One- and Two-Family Residential
(R2) Zone to the City Centre (CC1) Zone.


This is being proposed in order to allow for the construction of a 6-storey mixed-use building that would
consist of approximately 71 residential units and 175m2 (1,900 fe) of office space on the ground floor.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


 In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:


a)    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per residential
      unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:
               i.   $750 towards the Affordable Housing Fund;
              ii.   $2,850 toward the General Amenity Fund; and
             iii. $10.75 per m2 of commercial Gross Floor Area.


 b)    That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:
             i.   A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately managed
                  on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.


 c)    That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a section 219 covenant, registered in priority of
       all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
              i.   That all frontage improvements along Goldstream Avenue and Kristina Place are provided
                   as per Bylaw 1000, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to the issuance
                       of a Building Permit;
               ii.     That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building permit and
                       implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
            iii.       That a construction parking and traffic management plan be provided prior to the issuance
                       of a building permit, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
            iv.        That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
                       proposed residential building that ensures parking is assigned and tied to each unit created
                       in accordance with the minimum required parking stalls as per the zoning bylaw.
               v.      That no occupancy permit be issued for the proposed building until a strata plan for the
                       building has been registered, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer.

                                                                                                     October 5, 2020
                                                                                                        Page 3 of 16



Council has authorized the Director of Planning to issue the following variances within the Form and
Character Development Permit:
a. That the exterior side yard setback be reduced from 4.0m to 2.0.m.
b. That the interior side yard setback be reduced from 3.0m to 2.0m.
c. That the minimum distance of an unenclosed surface parking space to a lot line abutting a highway be
     reduced from 3.0m to 2.0m.
d.   That the minimum landscaped area between surface parking stalls and rear lot line be reduced from
     3.0m to 2.0m.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community City Centre designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Resident on Fairway Ave — Concerns with development and others on Goldstream 1.5km, roughly 1000-
1500 new units. Traffic, bus and overdevelopment without sufficient infrastructure. There needs to be more
thought out collaboration on the heels of Goldstream Road and Fairway Ave, 250+ units. Goldstream is over
capacity. When COVID lifts it's going to be a nightmare.

Resident on Kingswood Rd — First concern is a decrease in home value, our home is brand new, we are
concerned about what we are going to do. Second, the scale of the building dwarfs anything around it, it is
built in the centre of the neighbourhood. The development will destroy trees. Third, there are several old
large Douglas fir trees, you should study to see what's living in them. Need to try and keep them. The plans
for foliage on border of Kingswood Rd need to ensure they provide privacy and in short term, not wait 20
years for the trees to grow. There are traffic issues, speeding, using roundabout to turn around, parking
overflow onto the street. We are concerned about the safety of neighbourhood children and dogs. You are
tearing apart the community. This was bought and built, it was supposed to be residential.

Mayor Young asked about the size of the trees and confirmed that they can plant larger trees.

Resident #1 on Goldstream Avenue - We would like a sound barrier fence put up, and our driveway to be
moved from the front of Goldstream Ave to Kingsway Rd at the Developer's cost.

Mayor Young—Would like to see a sound barrier fence.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.




Resident on Kristina PI — The design is inappropriate. I bought 20 years ago on a single family lot. Young
families with young kids are now put in danger. I don't know how we can have this many without sewers.

                                                                                                       October 5, 2020
                                                                                                          Page 4 of 16



We oppose if passed and will probably block or protest.

M. Mahovlich, Direct of Engineering - advised that it is the developer who will pay for the extension of the
sewer to the development.

Resident #1 on Goldstream spoke again saying that their tenant gave notice because of this development.

Another resident has been here for 50 years or more and is seeing a complete loss of places to build or rent.
This is the path that Surrey, BC took, look where that went.

Resident #2 on Kingswood spoke again — the development is on the Developer's bill to pay for sewer. Seems
we are being held hostage, if you want sewer you have to allow buildings entitled to the same access to
sewers. There is a 2 nd petition signed that has been dropped off in addition to letters and emails.

M. Mahovlich, Direct of Engineering - this means the sewer will be extended to the area sooner than the
City's timeline and at the cost of the developer rather than the City.

Braden Hutchins, Director of Corporate Services — Confirmed all documents have been received and are
included in the Public Hearing package considered by Council.

Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the Public Hearing
for Bylaw No. 1905 closed at 5:59 p.m.

That Council:


1.   Whereas:


        A. The non-medicinal use of cannabis and cannabis related products has historically been
           prohibited byfederal law in Canada and, as a result, has historically been prohibited by the City
           under its Zoning Bylaw No. 300;
        B. On October 17, 2018, the Federal Government legalized the non-medicinal use of cannabis and
           cannabis products;

                                                                                                     March 18^ 2019
                                                                                                           Page 6 of 8


         C. The Federal Government and the Provincial Government have developed a regulatory
            framework for the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medicinal use;
         D. The City wishes to authorize the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products within its
            boundaries, but recognizes that there are challenges associated with it doing so;
         E. The City issued the Request for Proposals for the Retail Sales of Cannabis and Cannabis Related
            Products to seek proposals from individuals and organizations interested in undertaking the
            retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medicinal use within the City's boundaries,
            and required that proposals include details as to how the challenges with the retail sale of
            cannabis and cannabis products would be addressed;
         F. The City received and reviewed over 30 proposals in response to the Request For Proposals, and
              identified Clarity Cannabis BC Ltd.'s proposal as one that best addressed the challenges with the
              retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products; and,
         G. Clarity Cannabis BC Ltd. is committed to assisting the City and taking positive steps to address
            the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products.

              Now therefore be it resolved that Council issue Temporary Use Permit TUP19-0001 to Clarity
              Cannabis BC Ltd. for it to operate a Cannabis Retail Store at #101 - 693 Hoffman Avenue
              subject to the terms and conditions In the Temporary Use Permit as presented.

             Bylaw No. 1869, 2020".

The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1869 at 5:35 pm, and read a statennent to inform
those present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Kim Mohns has applied to amend the to amend the
zoning of 2865 Carlow Road from the R2 (One and Two Family) Zone to the RM7A (Medium Density
Apartment A) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a townhouse complex comprised of
approximately 9 units.                  .

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. $3,800 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;

2. $1000 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Fund;

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

The Acting Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Wil Peereboom of Victoria Design Group, on behalf of the applicant - Introduced the development, and
described how the design is intended to keep cars at the rear of the property and increase street presence.

Resident on Rodnev Road - Requested more information about onsite parking, and stated that they are in
favour of the development if parking is sufficient.

Applicant from the Victoria Design Group - Responded that there will be 2 parking spaces for each unit in
     the garage, plus 3 guest spaces, and 5 spaces along the curb.

Acting Mayor Szpak called a second time for presentations.

None.

Hearing for Bylaw No. 1869 closed at 5:40 p.m.

The City Planner advised that Irwin Consulting Ltd. has applied on behalf of Latoria Holdings Ltd. to amend
the Official Community Plan designation of 866 Latoria from Agricultural Strategy Lands to Hillside or
Shoreline and to rezone the lands from AG1 (Agriculture 1) to the RR6 (Rural Residential 6) Zone and the
RM2A (Attached Housing) Zone to permit the development of approximately 18 single-family lots and 30-
unit townhouse site.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:


                i.   $6,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
               ii.  $1,000 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
        as a bonus for increased density per one-family lot created;

        and
              iii. $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
              iv.    $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund.
        as a bonus for increased density per townhouse unit created.

        And


                   v.   $136,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

        as a condition for removing land from the ALR.

That, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the applicant agrees to register a covenant, which agrees to the following:

       vi.    A 2.0m wide road dedication be provided along Latoria Road;
      vii.    A 15m wide road dedication be provided for the proposed new road;
      viii.   That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provide to the satisfaction of
              the Director of Engineering;
       ix.    That all municipal works and third party utility services are installed within municipal road
              dedication;
        x.    That a storm water management plan be provided, which demonstrates the required onsite
              detention, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
       xi.    That notification be provided stating the properties are close to agricultural operations and
              the South Vancouver Rangers property, both of which may generate nuisances;
      xii.    That a tree protection plan, and the removal of any hazardous trees, is provided prior to
              subdivision approval.
      xiii.   That the Park area is dedicated to the City at the time of subdivision and that the applicant
              completes improvements within this Park to the satisfaction of the Parks Manager.

As part of this rezoning, Council direct staff to prepare a zoning bylaw amendment to the RR6 (Rural
Residential 6) Zone as per the following:


              a)    By permitting a secondary suite within a one-family dwelling or within an accessory
                    building on lots that are 500m2 or greater and in accordance with Section 3.08.

                                                                                                     May 22"d, 2018
                                                                                                       Page 3 of 16


As part of this rezoning, Council direct staff to prepare a zoning bylaw amendment to the RM2A (Attached
Housing) Zone as per the following:


         a)    That buildings in the RM2A Zone shall not exceed a floor area ratio of 0.75;

         b)    That the floor area ratio may be increased to 1.0, if the owner:

                   a. Pays to the City the amount specified in Column 4 of Table 1 of Schedule AD, prior to
                      issuance of a building permit.

         c)    That the floor area ratio may be increased to 1.5 if the owner provides 50% of the parking
               spaces in an underground or under building parking structure, subject to compliance with the
               density bonus provisions.

Council direct staff to forward the proposed subdivision plan and buffering plan to the Agricultural Land
Commission and request that they accept the proposed plans as satisfying their agricultural edge planning
condition for ALR exclusion.

Council authorize the Director of Planning to issue the following variances within the required
Development Permit for 866 Latoria Road:


        a)    That the minimum front yard setback be reduce to 3.0m (13 ft);

        c)    That the minimum exterior side yard setback be reduced to 3.0m (13 ft); and
        d)    That the minimum rear yard setback be reduced to 5.5m (18 ft).

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1721 at 5:30 p.m.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his
or her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Acting Mayor Councillor Sahlstrom
advised that after everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else
who wishes to be heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared
closed.

The City Planner advised that Rachael Sansom of Turnerlane Developments has applied on behalf of

                                                                                              September 5th, 2017
                                                                                                     Page 2 of 16


Meaford Holdings to amend the zoning of 732 Meaford Avenue from the CS1, Service Commercial, Zone
to the MU1A, Mixed Use Residential Commercial, Zone.

This is being proposed in order to align the zoning of the subject with that of the parcels south of the
subject property at 720 and 724 Meaford in order to allow for the construction of a 6 storey residential
apartment building on the properties.

This proposal is consistent with the properties' City Centre designation, within Langford's Official
Community Plan.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

As a bonus for increased density, the applicant has agreed to provide the following in accordance with
Council policy

1. $2,562 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund and
2. $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom called a first time for presentations.

None were presented.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom called a second time for presentations.

None were presented.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Acting Mayor
officially declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1721 closed at 5:31 p.m.

That Council direct staff to prepare a bylaw to amend the text of "Area 2" of the CD6 (Comprehensive
Development — Bear Mountain) Zone to permit the development of townhouses at a maximum density of
50 dwelling units per hectare (20 dwelling units per acre) on the property at 2500 Echo Valley Drive,
subject to the following terms and conditions:

        a)   That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing:

                           i.      A detailed site plan illustrating the proposed development and two
                                   routes for access to and egress from the site;
                           ii.     A stormwater management plan to the satisfaction of the Director of
                                   Engineering and the Approval Officer;
                           iii.    Confirmation of adequate water, fire flow and sanitary sewer capacities
                                   to serve the proposed development;

        b) That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 Covenant, registered in
           priority of all other charges on title, that agrees:

             i.        That all frontage improvements, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, be
                       constructed prior to subdivision approval or Building Permit issuance, whichever
                       occurs first;

             ii.       That any on- or off-site improvements required by the stormwater management plan
                       be implemented, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to

                       established prior to any construction on the site;

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1784 and Bylaw no. 1785 at 5:31 pm, and read a
statement to inform those present of the public hearing procedure.


Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Kevin Parker of Draycor Developments has applied on
behalf of Don and Patricia Gordon to amend the Official Community Plan designation from Agricultural to
Hillside or Shoreline and to amend the zoning from AG1 (Agricultural 1) Zone to RS4 (Residential Small Lot
4) Zone for the property located at 734 Latoria Rd.


This is being proposed in order to allow for subdivision and future residential development.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

                                                                                                   January 21st, 2019
                                                                                                        Page 2 of 14




In support of these applications, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per single
      family equivalent (SFE) created, prior to subdivision approval:

      i)     $1,000 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
      ii)    $6,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

2.   That the applicant provides, as a condition of removing land from the Agricultural Land Reserve, $6.72
     per m2 of gross land area being rezoned towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund prior to subdivision
     approval for the creation of more than one lot located north of the SPEA and more than one lot located
     south of the SPEA.

3.   That the applicant provides the following prior to Public Hearing:

     i)      A technical memorandum regarding proposed stormwater management for the development,
             to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

4.   That the applicant registers a Section 219 Covenant, in priority of all other charges on title, prior to
     Bylaw Adoption that agrees to:

     i)      Construct full frontage improvements, in accordance with Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the
             satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to subdivision approval or Building Permit
             issuance, whichever occurs first;

     ii)     Prepare a construction management parking plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of
             Engineering, prior to Building Permit issuance;

     iii)    Prepare a detailed stormwater management plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of
             Engineering, prior to subdivision approval or Building Permit issuance, whichever occurs first;

     iv)    Construct any above- or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or other
            servicing requirements required by the approved stormwater management plan, in accordance
            with Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to
            subdivision approval or Building Permit issuance, whichever occurs first;

     v)     Construct a 2. 0 m (6.6ft) wide gravel multi-use trail along the Latoria Road frontage of the
            subject property and extending north into Desmond Park and east to the property at 720, and
            complete all associated landscaping and remediation work, to the satisfaction of the Parks
            Manager, prior to subdivision approval or Building Permit issuance, whichever occurs first;

     vi)    Acknowledge that the site is in proximity to agricultural areas and the South Vancouver Island
            Rangers gun range, and that these uses may create general noise, odour and other nuisances,
            and agree that the owner and all future owners assume all risk and annoyance of such
            nuisances; and

    vii)     Dedicate approximately 17.5% of the property at 734 Latoria Road to the City, and $55,000
             cash-in-lieu of open space to the General Amenity Reserve Fund, prior to subdivision approval.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

Resident on Goldspur Road — Thanked Mayor and Council and relayed support for the affordable housing
but does not support RS4 as it does not fit with the community. Resident thinks the city should maintain the
same zoning as said in 2004. Resident raised concerns about riparian infractions, that broader services are
not being supported, is also concerned that neighbourhood parks are not being funded and that the
neighbourhood is not being represented by elected officials and askes that Council to pursue RRGA.

Will Perrell, Victoria Design — If keeping the same zoning, could get the same number lots as the proposed
reszoing. This is just how to do it best (# of lots will be the same). Trying to make the design appealing.
Parking will not spill over into other developments.

Resident on Whimfield Terrace — Not opposed to development but is opposed to RS4. There is not enough
density to what is being developed. Mentioned to council that lots will be sold as bare land. Resident is
concerned that there is not enough room and that secondary suites will create issues for parking. There is
not enough transit for the increase and no greenspace or park developments.

Resident on Wendev Drive — Supports houses but doesn't support RS4 as it doesn't fit into the
neighbourhood. Where are the trees in the picture? Where is extra parking, what is happening to the creek?

Applicant — Confirmed that all houses have to have a development permit to control form and character
and clarified that RS4 and RS6 set backs are the same.

Les Biola, Goldstream Ave —Stated that the average household income to buy in Langford is $140,000. The
city is trying to balance affordability with development. Draycor has already built a lot of houses on Latoria
Road and thanked them.

Resident on Wendey Drive — Is not opposed to development just the zoning and smaller lots. Parking is a
concern, as well as traffic and safety.

Applicant — Provided clarification on parking (4 cars per household) and provide some parking amounts as
RRGA. If it remains a strata, the public isn't welcome.

Resident on Desmond Drive — Asked if 4 parking spots included the garage.

Mayor Young clarified that yes, the 4 parking spaces included the garage.

Resident asked for clarification about the park and school acquisition.

Mayor Young clarified that it's a School District process and not public information.

Resident said they do not support the bylaw amendment. After the Planning and Zoning meeting, Draycor

                                                                                                     January 21st, 2019
                                                                                                          Page 4 of 14


was to provide information to neighbours: Why not RRGA, traffic concerns, riparian area concerns, impact
to neighbourhood. Draycor had a meeting on November 26, 2018, but have questions still unsettled (e.g.
 no riparian professional present). Walked through concerns about each of the above questions. RRGA
doesn't provide same number of lots as RS4. Development is not keeping with previous decisions regarding
zoning. Draycor is unable to answer environmental concerns questions. Douglas fir concerns needs further
looking into. Water flow has not been adequately looked at. Concerned about riparian report methodology.
Brought examples of species that are living in the water. Studies she conducted shows continuous life which
support the trout. Concern lookout brook is needed as a ditch, not a stream as legally required. Bylaw No.
