     7.1    Early Guidance for Development Connected to the Strategic Plan Update

canonical_motions.agenda_item_title: Early Guidance for Development Connected to the Strategic Plan Update
canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
THAT Council support in principle the following interim measure to provide Early
            Guidance for development applications:








      1. HIGH QUALITY GROWTH AND DENSITY:

      Council's intention is to support growth with an emphasis on successful urban
      community-building, while increasingly emphasizing the quality of new higher density
      development, particularly in the context of livability, sustainability, affordability, and
      development viability. The achievement of high-quality urban density will emphasize
      urban design and architectural design that results in engaging street-level activation and
      vibrancy, and an ambitious street tree canopy. Where taller buildings are proposed,
      floor plates should be relatively slim and well separated to avoid the individual or
      cumulative effects of excessive upper-floor massing.

      In addition to design quality, considerations of high-quality urban density should
      include, where beneficial and viable, some or all of the following:

          •   Amenities supporting livability/quality of urban life at the building, block, and
              neighbourhood scale.

          •   Integration of existing mature, viable site trees where feasible relative to tree
              location, site conditions, development viability and other public interest
              considerations.

          •   Consideration of relative affordability opportunities.

          •   Inclusion of 2-3-bedroom apartments for families as well as other family
              supports such as in-suite storage, in-building amenities etc.

          •   Green design opportunities relative to architectural design and sustainable
              energy sources over-and-above City requirements.

          •   Avoidance of excessive vehicle parking, and strategic provision of enhanced
              supports for alternatives to vehicle ownership and use, including diverse urban
              biking options, walking, public transit use and carshare.

          •   Strategic supports in housing and mobility for accessibility.


      2. LESS IMPACTFUL, MORE LIVABLE CONSTRUCTION:

      To mitigate the construction impacts of medium and high-density growth on existing
      neighbours and neighbourhoods in a rapidly and continuously changing city,
      applications should propose and implement a well-considered "good neighbour
      commitment" that reflects established high-quality practice in maintaining urban
      livability during construction.

4.     PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

       Greg, Florence Lake Rd - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed concern regarding the tax increase
       influencing landlords to sell their investments. Expressed opposition to the tax increase.








L. Morton, Phelps Ave - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed opposition to the tax increase. The
speaker inquired about questions that arose from the previous Special Council meeting of May
8, 2023. Expressed concern about the new proposed RCMP hires and where will they be housed
and where will the funding come from. The speaker inquired about the purchase of the YMCA,
why would you consider buying the YMCA without a fulsome business case prepared with
options? Which institution would we borrow the funds to purchase the YMCA? If you are not
considering buying the YMCA this year, why is it included in the budget?

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded that multiple municipalities are responsible for
the West Shore RCMP detachment. A plan is being devised during construction. The purchase of
the YMCA is based on the City's is obligation to pay a $30,000,000,000 lease. Purchasing the
building would mean that after the lease, the City will own the building. The purchasing of the
YMCA building will come before Council at a future date.

R.Louie, Bellamy Rd - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed feelings of being defeated and
disappointment. Expressed concern regarding rental costs increasing. Expressed concern that
long-time residents may leave the City. Expressed concern regarding not having a referendum
about the YMCA. Expressed that staff increases should have been deferred. Expressed that there
should have restructured the increase of the firefighters being hired. Expressed concern that
Council did bot negotiate the budget enough for the public. Expressed concern regarding the
RCMP building. Expressed opposition to the tax increase.

S.Sifert, Walfred Rd - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Speaker is a long-time resident of the City of Langford.
Expressed opposition to the tax increase. Expressed feelings of being dismissed and excluded
from the process. Expressed concern regarding the amount development. Expressed concern
regarding the process of public participation.

J. Relph, Knotty Pine Rd - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed support for the budget.

M. Morton, Phelps Ave - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed concern regarding the budget process.
Expressed concern regarding the removal of the committee process. Expressed concern
regarding the lack of response to their questions.

E. Wright, Commander Crt - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed concern regarding the lack of
leadership or direction in serving the public best interests in the budget process. Expressed
concern regarding the process being transparent and fulsome. Expressed concern that the
process excluded the public. Expressed that staff dictated the budget. Expressed opposition to
the budget.

M. Wignall, Selwyn Rd - re: items 5.1& 5.2 - The speaker echoed comments from previous
speakers. Expressed that the public is being dismissed. Expressed that the process was not
collaborative enough. Expressed criticism to the process, that the process was not transparent.

L. Foxall, Players Dr - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed opposition to the budget. Expressed
concern that Council are not being attentive to the public speakers. Expressed that the budget
was for staff, not the public. Expressed that raising amenity fees will cut taxes 6%. Expressed
that Council used 1.7 million from reserves to bring down the increase.

N. Johal, Walfred PI - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed concern regarding comments made by
Councillor Yacucha. Expressed opposition to the tax increase. The speaker inquired about how









much taxes are collected from the YMCA. The speaker inquired about the maintenance fees for
the YMCA. Expressed concern about the cost of the YMCA.

Councillor Yacucha responded by explaining the comment that the percentage increase and how
it impacts a particular household.

Motion was made to extend the public participation.

Nicholas Johal, Walfred PI - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed concerns that the tax increase will
cause undue burden to seniors, low-income households, and young adults. Expressed concern
about the RCMP building. Expressed that developers should pay their fair share. Expressed that
developers should support the infrastructure of the City. Expressed concern regarding
transparency of the budget process. Expressed concern regarding the public ideas being
dismissed. Expressed support for public safety but is concerned about the lack of support given
to the RCMP.

R. MacBeth, Rita Rd - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed concern that public suggestions were not
reflected in the budget. Expressed concern that time attending Council meetings as been in vain.
Expressed concern regarding the elimination of the Administration and Finance Committee
before budget deliberations. Expressed concern about the purchase of the YMCA. Inquired
about the use of the term class.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded that the term class comes from BC Assessment
and that they have 9 classes to determine properties.

C. Weatherston, Cressida Cres - re: items 5.1 & 5.2 - Expressed support for the tax increase. The
speaker stated that other municipalities have the same average percentage increase.

B. Sahlstrom, Walfred Rd - re: item 5.1 - The speaker inquired how the tax increase will affect
businesses.

M. Dillabaugh, Director of Finance responded to previous questions. YMCA does not pay
property tax. Items on the budget will have due diligence through the Council process.

canonical_motions.agenda_item_title: Sustainable Development Advisory Committee Meeting Resolutions - August 12, 2024
canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
THAT Council:
                          1. Proceed with consideration of First, Second, and Third Reading of Bylaw
                             No. 2192, following public notification, to amend the zoning designation







of the property located at 967A Isabell Avenue from RS1 and R2 to RT1
subject to the following terms and conditions:

a.   That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the
     following contributions per dwelling unit, prior to the issuance of a
     building permit:

     i.    $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and

     ii. $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;

b. That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a release of
   the covenant that was previously registered under CA5774371
   through Bylaw No. 1646, and registers a Section 219 covenant in
   priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

     i.    That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw
           No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
           Engineering prior to the issuance of a building permit:

           1. Full frontage improvements; and

           2. A storm water management plan.

     ii.   That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw
           No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
           Engineering prior to any land alterations:

           1. A mitigation plan;

           2. A construction parking and deliveries management; and

           3. An erosion and sediment control plan.

     iii. That, prior to the issuance of a Development Permit, the
          developer completes the process of road closure and
          disposition, and consolidates approximately 163.4m2 of
          municipal road right of way into the subject property;

     iv. That a separate covenant be registered, prior to issuance of a
         building permit for the proposed development, agreeing that
         the garages are to be used for the parking of vehicles and not
         the storage of items preventing the parking of vehicles therein,
         in favour of the strata;

     v.    That a separate covenant is registered, prior to issuance of a
           building permit for the proposed development agreeing that
           the strata be responsible for maintaining the boulevard
           landscaping from the back of the sidewalk with the exception of
           boulevard trees;









      vi. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete
          that meets or exceeds the weighted average Global Warming
          Potential targets based on Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix
          data, and that prior to the issuance of a Building Permit the
          applicant shall provide a Type III Environmental Product
          Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global
          Warming Potential value and confirming that the proposed
          development meets the requirements of Low Carbon Concrete
          Policy POL-0167-PLAN;

     vii. That electric heat pumps are installed in each townhouse unit;

     viii. That tree protection measures, inclusive of tree protection
           fencing, are implemented prior to commencement of work to
           protect the trees identified for retention in the arborist report
           throughout the construction period. A written confirmation
           from the project arborist that the tree protection fencing was
           installed shall be submitted to the City, prior to the
           commencement of work, to the satisfaction of the Director of
           Parks, Recreation and Facilities;

     ix. That the large diameter cypress tree currently existing within
         the frontage shall be retained. If the tree cannot be retained
         under the current proposal, the proposal shall be adjusted
         accordingly to ensure preservation of the tree. If mutually
         agreed upon by the developer and the City of Langford that the
         tree cannot be preserved, then a cash contribution based on
         the assessed value of the tree shall apply and be payable by the
         developer to the City of Langford, prior to occupancy permit. If
         the tree is removed without the consent of the City of Langford,
         the developer shall provide a cash contribution to the City equal
         to three (3) times the assessed value of the tree.



2. Amend the text of Schedule AD of the Zoning Bylaw No. 300 to
remove the amenity contributions related to Bylaw No. 1646;



3. Direct staff to prepare a Bylaw to proceed with the road closure and
disposition of approximately 163.4m2 of municipal road right of way as
shown on the Road Closure Plan, attached to this report.



4. Authorize the Director of Development Services to issue the following
variance in the Form and Character Development Permit:

i.   Section 6.28.07(d) be varied to reduce the minimum rear yard
     setback from the required 5.5m to 5.0m.

Whereas Rick Hansen Foundation Accessibility CertificationTM (RHFAC) is
             a national rating system that measures and certifies the level of meaningful access of
             buildings and sites and the Rick Hansen Foundation found that 64% of Canadians have a
             disability or take care of a person with a disability.







             And Whereas, one of the key findings of a 2020 Cost Comparison Feasibility Study issued
             by HCMA Architecture + Design was that when meeting the National Building Code there
             was a cost increase of 1% to achieve Rick Hansen Foundation Certified Gold which
             reinforces that "accessibility can be achieved with minimal cost impact through
             commitment to thoughtful/universal design".

             Therefore, Langford Council directs staff to consider Rick Hansen Foundation
             Accessibility CertificationTM (RHFAC) when completing the upcoming review of
             Langford's Design Guidelines.

       PUBLIC HEARINGS


       4.1     BYLAW NO. 2096

               "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 690 (2089 Champions Way), Bylaw No. 2096,
               2022"



      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2096 at 5:37 pm.

      Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohnnann advised that Devon Skinner has applied on
      behalf of 1289877 BC Ltd. to amend the text of the Resort Community of Bear Mountain
      2 (RCBM2) Zone to increase the maximum permitted tow/nhouse density from 1 unit per
      285 m2 to 1 unit per 214 m2 for the property located at 2089 Champions Way.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of up to 29 townhouse
      units.

      Council is concurrently considering a Development Variance Permit application to
      increase the maximum permitted height of townhouse buildings on the property from
      9m to between 9.7m and 11.4m as well as to reduce the width of a maneuvering aisle in
      a building family residential building from 6.7m to 5.8m.

      In accordance with the existing provisions of the RCBM2 Zone, the applicant will provide
      a contribution of $1,525 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.

      This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Village Centre designation.

      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
      Government Act.

      Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

      The applicant gave a presentation, providing an overview of the project site, project
      components, variances requested, and site concepts.

      H. Bereer, 2034 Hedgestone Way, expressed concerns about the lack of sidewalk and
      the proposed density.

      D. Van SIvke. 2103 Champions Wav. expressed support for the proposal and
      commended the applicant's responses to his concerns.

      N. Young, 1312 Champions Court, expressed support for the proposal.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations. There being none, he
      declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2096 closed at 6:11 pm.

4.2   BYLAW NO. 2091

      "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 686, (2786, 2792, 2798 Scafe Road and 821,
      825 Wren Place) Bylaw No. 2091, 2022"

      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2091 at 6:12 pm.

      Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Nick Bray has applied on
      behalf of Rick Genovese of 1232189 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 2786, 2792, 2798
      Scafe Road and 821, 825 Wren Place from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2)
      Zone to the City Centre 2 (CC2) Zone and to amend the text of the CC2 zone to increase



the allowable height of a building or structure from 4 storeys to 6 storeys for the subject
properties only.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a six-storey residential
building containing approximately 114 units.

Prior to Public Hearing, the applicant has provided a technical memo from an engineer
that verifies stormwater can be adequately managed on-site for the proposed
development, which has been approved by the Director of Engineering AND a memo by
a Landscape Architect that examines existing trees on site and in the frontage to provide
comment on potential tree retention, which has been approved by the Director of
Planning.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. The following contributions as a bonus for increased density:
a. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
b. $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
2. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan, as well as a
construction parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000
standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

3. That the five subject properties be consolidated prior to issuance of a Development
Permit for Form and Character;

4. That prior to issuance of a Development Permit, the design of the 3 m walkway
corridor be approved by the Director of Parks and a 3 m Statutory Right of Way be
registered on title of the consolidated property;

5. That no occupancy permit be issued for the proposed building until a strata plan for
the building has been registered;

6. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
proposed development that ensure residential parking is allocated to each unit and
visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in exchange for
compensation separate from that of a residential unit;

7. That all concrete used on-site will be produced using post-industrial C02
mineralization technology, or equivalent which offers concrete with lower embodied
C02 than all other competing bids, and that prior to the issuance of a Building Permit
the applicant shall provide a product-specific Type III Environmental Product Declaration
that is 3rd party verified specifying the total embodied carbon content of concrete;

8. Council also has, by resolution, authorized the Director of Planning and Subdivision to
issue a variance to reduce the rear lot line setback from the required 3.0 m to 2.0 m in
the Form and Character Development Permit.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Governmen t Act



      Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

      The applicant gave a presentation; providing an overview of the design, location, and
      proposed amenities.

      P. Hamilton. 636 Granderson Road, posed questions about how the proposal will
      address mobility concerns.

      M. Wagner. #104-2669 DeviHe Road, expressed concerns about deviations from the
      Official Community Plan.

      P. Hamilton. 636 Granderson Road, posed additional questions on mobility issues.

      K. Guirv. 539 Phelps Avenue, expressed concerns about the proposed building setback
      along the pathways.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Yourig called for a third and final tinrie for presentations. There being none, he
      declared the Public Hearingfor Bylaw No. 2091 closed at 6:36 pm

      K. Delbrouck. 996 Fashoda Place, expressed support for the project, and expressed

      R. Lubberts, 806Stanehill Place, would like the application paused due to it being a

      M. Wellwood. 1015 Fashoda Place, expressed support for the project and expressed

           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 453, (2131, 2181, 2160, 2200, 2250, 2251, 2300,
           2350 Bear Mountain Pkwy; 2750 & 2751 Echo Valley Dr; 2588 Savory Rd; VIP87258 Lots 1-

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1622 at 7:04 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone

                                                                                       Regular Meeting of Council
                                                                                                  June 20th, 2016
                                                                                                     Page 2 of 21


has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Ron Coutre of Goldstream Heights Properties Ltd. and Southpoint Partners
Ltd. and Blair Robertson of Totangi Properties Ltd. have applied to amend the zoning of 2131, 2181, 2160,
2200, 2250, 2251, 2300, 2350 Bear Mountain Pkwy; 2750 & 2751 Echo Valley Dr; 2588 Savory Rd;
VIP87258 Lots 1-6 by amending the text of the CD12 (Comprehensive Development 12 — South Skirt
Mountain) Zone with respect to land use, an overall reduction in development density and amenity
contribution requirements.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. An amenity contribution of $2,000 per SFE towards the general amenity reserve fund to replace the
    existing amenity contribution requirements;
2. Construct park and trail improvements as required by the City;

The applicant is proposing that the existing Master Development Agreement registered on title of the
subject properties be revised as part of this application. A draft of the proposed new MDA is with the
City's solicitor for review. Some of the proposed changes include removing the following requirements:
    • The construction of a public plaza by 1410 dwelling units;
    • The establishment of at least 5 commercial or institutional uses in the zone by 1410 dwelling units;
    • The dedication of a firefighting training area;
    • The creation of a community garden;
    • Subsequent environmental reports/plans including: integrated pest management plan, retention
         of wildlife corridors and water quality monitoring of downstream waterbodies including Florence
         Lake and Spencer's Pond;
    • Specific green building requirements, including: use of permeable paving materials, energy
         efficiency rating level, On-site renewable energy system, diversion of at least 50% of construction
        waste and requirement for a third-party audit of development permit applications;

The applicant wishes to retain the requirement for the public plaza within the mixed-use core, but remove
the requirement for it to be constructed prior the development of more than 1410 dwelling units. A
concept plan would still be required prior to the issuance of any DP in Area IV — Mixed Use Core, and the
plaza would be constructed as part of the works approved for adjoining buildings.

There are four Areas of the CD12 Zone (IV, V-A, V-B and VI) that only, or primarily, permit commercial
uses. Area III also permits commercial uses as part of a mixed-use building. Due to this, there is minimal
risk that fewer than 5 commercial uses will be incorporated into the development.

The dedication of the firefighting training area and community garden were to occur within the lands
dedicated as open space, so the City may still allocate space for these uses if desired and/or needed.

The environmental reports/plans/conditions specified in the MDA can be secured where applicable as
part of the Development Permit or Subdivision approval processes.

                                                                                       Regular Meeting of Council
                                                                                                  June 20th, 2016
                                                                                                     Page 3 of 21


The applicant is proposing to retain the requirement to certify each building pursuant to a third-party
green building certification system (such as Built Green, LEED-NC, or similar), and proposes that Council
accept this as meeting the intent of creating a green development in lieu of the other more specific
requirements.

Finally, the MDA contains conditions that restrict development to a certain trigger point until various road
improvements are constructed. Once such improvement - the Leigh Road Interchange - has been
completed since this Agreement was first written, and another - the Echo Valley Dr connection to the
northern zone boundary adjoining the CD6 (Bear Mountain) Zone - has been deemed unnecessary as part
of a recent traffic impact assessment. Therefore, references to these works may be removed from this
MDA. Council is considering establishing a new Local Service Area to fund the Bear Mountain Parkway
construction, so references in the MDA to this road may be removed and/or adjusted should this LSA be
successful. In the event that the LSA is not created, the City can still require road construction from the
property owner at the time of subdivision.

The applicant has also requested that a new clause be inserted into the MDA which would allow certain
improvements such as playgrounds or trails constructed on open space land transferred to the City to be
DCC creditable.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood Centre, Hillside or Shoreline
and Business or Light Industrial designations and notifications and advertisements have been placed as
required by Council policy.

The City Planner advised that Ron Coutre of Goldstream Heights Properties Ltd. and Southpoint Partners
Ltd. and Blair Robertson of Totangi Properties Ltd. have applied to amend the zoning of 2131, 2181, 2160,
2200, 2250, 2251, 2300, 2350 Bear Mountain Pkwy; 2750 & 2751 Echo Valley Dr; 2588 Savory Rd;
VIP87258 Lots 1-6 by amending the text of the CD12 (Comprehensive Development 12 — South Skirt
Mountain) Zone with respect to land use, an overall reduction in development density and amenity
contribution requirements.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. An amenity contribution of $2,000 per SFE towards the general amenity reserve fund to replace the
    existing amenity contribution requirements;
2. Construct park and trail improvements as required by the City;

The applicant is proposing that the existing Master Development Agreement registered on title of the
subject properties be revised as part of this application. A draft of the proposed new MDA is with the
City's solicitor for review. Some of the proposed changes include removing the following requirements:
    • The construction of a public plaza by 1410 dwelling units;
    • The establishment of at least 5 commercial or institutional uses in the zone by 1410 dwelling units;
    • The dedication of a firefighting training area;
    • The creation of a community garden;
    • Subsequent environmental reports/plans including: integrated pest management plan, retention
         of wildlife corridors and water quality monitoring of downstream waterbodies including Florence
         Lake and Spencer's Pond;
    • Specific green building requirements, including: use of permeable paving materials, energy
         efficiency rating level, On-site renewable energy system, diversion of at least 50% of construction
        waste and requirement for a third-party audit of development permit applications;

The applicant wishes to retain the requirement for the public plaza within the mixed-use core, but remove
the requirement for it to be constructed prior the development of more than 1410 dwelling units. A
concept plan would still be required prior to the issuance of any DP in Area IV — Mixed Use Core, and the
plaza would be constructed as part of the works approved for adjoining buildings.

There are four Areas of the CD12 Zone (IV, V-A, V-B and VI) that only, or primarily, permit commercial
uses. Area III also permits commercial uses as part of a mixed-use building. Due to this, there is minimal
risk that fewer than 5 commercial uses will be incorporated into the development.

The dedication of the firefighting training area and community garden were to occur within the lands
dedicated as open space, so the City may still allocate space for these uses if desired and/or needed.

The environmental reports/plans/conditions specified in the MDA can be secured where applicable as
part of the Development Permit or Subdivision approval processes.

The applicant is proposing to retain the requirement to certify each building pursuant to a third-party
green building certification system (such as Built Green, LEED-NC, or similar), and proposes that Council
accept this as meeting the intent of creating a green development in lieu of the other more specific
requirements.

Finally, the MDA contains conditions that restrict development to a certain trigger point until various road
improvements are constructed. Once such improvement - the Leigh Road Interchange - has been
completed since this Agreement was first written, and another - the Echo Valley Dr connection to the
northern zone boundary adjoining the CD6 (Bear Mountain) Zone - has been deemed unnecessary as part
of a recent traffic impact assessment. Therefore, references to these works may be removed from this
MDA. Council is considering establishing a new Local Service Area to fund the Bear Mountain Parkway
construction, so references in the MDA to this road may be removed and/or adjusted should this LSA be
successful. In the event that the LSA is not created, the City can still require road construction from the
property owner at the time of subdivision.

The applicant has also requested that a new clause be inserted into the MDA which would allow certain
improvements such as playgrounds or trails constructed on open space land transferred to the City to be
DCC creditable.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood Centre, Hillside or Shoreline
and Business or Light Industrial designations and notifications and advertisements have been placed as
required by Council policy.

5.   PRESENTATIONS

     5.1    Urban Forest Management Plan - Tyler Searls, Diamond Head Consulting

            Tyler Searls, Diamond Head Consulting presented on the Urban Forest Management Plan
            and Bylaw No. 2206.

     5.2    Public Participation (Urban Forest Management Plan & Bylaw No. 2206 Only)

            B. White, Langford Resident - The speaker stated how impressed they were with the
            scope of the presentation. The speaker inquired about the development of Langford
            Heights and how will the Urban Forest Management Plan protect Millstream Creek.

            G. Willing, Colwood Resident - The speaker stated they are a City of Langford property
            owner. The speaker inquired about hiring an arborist. The speaker inquired about the
            protection of tress under 20 cm in diameter. The speaker inquired if Agricultural Land
            Reserves are exempt from Bylaw No. 2206. The speaker inquired about native species
            trees being protected. The speaker inquired about a tree inventory on private land. The
            speaker inquired about risk management in regard to fire.

            L.Foxall, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired about the City of Langford's insurance
            coverage. The speaker expressed concern regarding the tree permit process and the
            potential cost to the public.

            S. Geary, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern regarding the Urban Forest
            Management Plan and the protection of trees during the development permitting
            process. The speaker expressed concern regarding Bylaw No. 2206 compared to other
            municipalities. The speaker expressed concern for the protection of native species.

            M. Brooke, Langford Resident - The speaker stated they were pleased with the
            implementation of the Urban Forest Management Plan and the consideration of hiring
            an arborist. The speaker expressed concern regarding limiting maple trees in the City.

            M. Morton, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern about the cost of tree
            removal.

            N.Johal, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired about the cost of tree removal. The
            speaker expressed concern regarding the liability of dangerous trees.

            J. McGee, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed concern regarding the previous
            removal of trees and the required replacement. The speaker expressed concern
            regarding the lack of control of their own property.







Councillor Harder left the meeting at 8:05 pm and returned at 8:06 pm.

L. Plomp, Langford Resident - The speaker stated they were encouraged to see the draft
of the Urban Forest Management Plan. The speaker stated that protection of trees does
not have to be at the expense of slowing development. The speaker requested that
Council make changes to the Official Community Plan and the development permit
process. The speaker requested long term protection of trees. The speaker requested
that Bylaw No. 2206 contain a list of trees that are significant assets or heritage trees
and include a penalty if any damaged or loss. The speaker requested a fund be
established from fines to assist low-income households in the removal of trees. The
speaker approves the hiring of an arborist. The speaker stated that fines for tree removal
by developers should not be overlooked.

K. Dahlberg, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed support for the Urban Forest
Management Plan. The speaker expressed concern regarding the 20 cm diameter
threshold for tree removal.

S. Plank, Langford Resident - The speaker stated they appreciates the support for tree
protection. The speaker requested Council develop on previously developed areas. The
speaker requested Council change the required setbacks and tree protection in the
development permit process. The speaker expressed concern regarding the protection
of native species. The speaker supports the hiring of an arborist.

B.Sahlstrom, Langford Resident - The speaker does not support the tree permitting
process. The speaker expressed concern regarding trees on City property. The speaker
requested public notification of the new tree permit process.

At 8:16 pm Council made a motion to extend the Urban Forest Management Plan public
participation, please see below.

Nicholas Johal, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired about the loss of tree canopy.
The speaker inquired about the thermal imaging used in the report. The speaker
inquired about what requirements make a tree canopy.

R. Coutre, Langford Resident - The speaker thanked Council and staff for allowing the
West Shore Developers Association to be a part of the development of the draft Urban
Forest Management Plan. The speaker requested section 6 d. of Bylaw No. 2206 include
retaining walls, driveways, sidewalks and pathways. The speaker stated that the West
Shore Developers Association welcome a conversation regarding changes to the
development permit process.

C.Aram, Langford Resident - The speaker expressed gratitude for the work done to bring
forth the draft Urban Forest Management Plan. The speaker expressed concern
regarding the tree protection in the development permit process. The speaker supports
development on previously developed areas. The speaker supports the hiring of an
arborist.

W. Hobbs, Langford Resident - The speaker inquired regarding the replanting of trees
when trees are removed during new road construction.

                                   ii. $660 per single family home or half duplex towards the

                                   iii. $3,660 per townhouse unit towards the General Amenity
                                        Reserve Fund; and
                                   iv. $3,960 per single family home or half duplex towards the
                                       General Amenity Reserve Fund.


                              b. That the applicant registers, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a road
                                 dedication plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
                              c.   That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, registers a Section 219

i.   That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw
     No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
     Engineering, prior to the issuance of a building permit:
     1. Full frontage improvements; and
     2. A storm water management plan.


ii. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw
    No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
    Engineering prior to any land alteration:
     1. A construction parking management plan; and
     2. A mitigation plan.


iii. That the applicant shall apply for subdivision utilizing the plan
     demonstrated to Council during the rezoning process, or one
     that is substantially similar demonstrating that all new lots
     created are below 280 m2 in size;

    that meets or exceeds the weighted average Global Warming
    Potential targets based on Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix
    data, and that prior to the issuance of a Building Permit the

The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1904 at 5:31 pm, and read a statement to inform
those present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that the following Omnibus No.51 contemplates amending
the text of the Zoning Bylaw to add a new downtown zone. The new CC1, City Centre 1, Zone will be applied
to properties that are outside of the core Goldstream Avenue area, or main thoroughfares such as Peatt or
Jacklin Road.


This is being proposed in order to create a zone with regulations special to the downtown that will support
the recent changes made to Langford's Design Guidelines for the Downtown


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.


The Acting Mayor called a first time for presentations.

None presented.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom called a second time for presentations.

Resident on Hockley Ave— Called to express support for the Bylaw. Stated that their concerns had been
addressed and they are in support

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the
Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1904 closed at 5:42 p.m.

        b)   BYLAW NO. 1920
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 597, (Omnibus No. 53—Various

those present of the public hearing procedure.

            Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Michelle Mahovlich has
           applied on behalf of Patrick Stephenson to amend the zoning of 3405 Happy Valley from
           the Rural Residential 2 (RR2) to the Residential Small Lot 1 (RS1) zone.
           This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 13 single-
           family lots.
           1. In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a
           bonus for increased density:
                a. $660 per small Lot to the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
                 b. $3,960 per small lot to the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
           2. That the applicant registers, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a road dedication plan, to the
           satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
           3. That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant,
           registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
           a. That frontage improvements along the extension of Vision Way, a stormwater
           management plan and a construction parking and traffic management plan are provided
           to Bylaw 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the
           issuance of a Building Permit;
           b. That full frontage improvements along Happy Valley Road will be provided and
           implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of
           Engineering prior to subdivision approval of "Proposed Lot A";
           c. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
           proposed development agreeing that the garages are to be used for the parking of
           vehicles and not the storage of items preventing the parking of vehicles therein;
           d. That, prior to commencement of work, tree protection measures inclusive of tree
           protection fencing are implemented to protect the trees identified for retention in the
           arborist report, and as confirmed by the Director of Parks, Recreation and Facilities with
           respect to the dedicated parkland, throughout the construction period;

6.2   BYLAW NO. 2135

      "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 701, (Omnibus No. 63 —Text Amendment to
      Remove Clause Requiring Second Parking Stall for Three-Bedroom Units), Bylaw No.
      2135, 2023".

      Acting Mayor Wagner opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2135 at 7:58 pm.

       Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Bylaw 2135 proposes to amend
      Zoning Bylaw 300 by reducing the number of off-street parking stalls for apartment units
      that have more than two-bedrooms.
      The requirement for the provision of an additional parking space for these larger
      apartment units was added approximately 5 years ago. Since this time, the city has
       received feedback that this requirement added a significant barrier to construction these
      larger units due to many factors, including the physical amount of land required to
      incorporate the additional parking spaces and the cost of constructing the additional
      parking. These have pushed the costs associated with constructing larger units much
      higher, and arguably out of the affordability range for many wishing to live in that type of
      home, making it more viable for a project to incorporate a larger number of smaller
      units for the same amount of parking required for a smaller project with larger units.
      Over the same time, the housing crisis has intensified, with single-family homes and
      even townhouses becoming increasingly out of reach for many households requiring
      more than 2 bedrooms to meet their needs. Due to this, it is becoming more important
      to incorporate larger units that can accommodate larger households into multi-family
      buildings.
      Council may further wish to note that since the introduction of this Bylaw, staff have
      experienced an increase in the number of current and pending development proposals
      that wish to incorporate three-bedroom units.
      The proposed amendment would be consistent with the City's Official Community Plan.
      Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government
      Act.

             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 594, (918 and 924 Jenkins Ave), Bylaw
             No. 1886, 2020".

                                                                                                      January 18, 2021
                                                                                                          Page 2 of 30


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1886 at 5:37 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Gary Brown has applied on behalf of 0981172 BC Ltd
and Paradise Homes Ltd to amend the zoning of 918 and 914 Jenkins Avenue from the R2 (One- and Two-
Family Residential) Zone to the RM7A (Medium Density Apartment A) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of two 24-unit apartment buildings.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per residential
   unit, prior to the issuance of a building permit:

         i. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
        ii. $3,660 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
      Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the Affordable Housing
      and Amenity Contribution Policy

2. That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of
   all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

        a.   That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided to the satisfaction of the
             Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a building permit;

        b. That a storm water management plan be provided prior to the issuance of a building permit and
           implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

        c.   That a construction parking and traffic management plan be provided prior to the issuance of a
             building permit, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

        d.   That the developer registers a strata plan, prior to the issuance of an occupancy permit, that
             creates individual strata titles for each residential unit;

        e.   That the required parking stalls for this development are allocated for the use by individuals in
             each unit, as required by Bylaw 300 and designated accordingly, and that the parking stalls are
             not sold or rented out individually;

        f.   That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall feature an
             energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to the parking space; and
                  i. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
                 ii. Where an electric vehicle energy management system is implemented (load sharing),
                     the Director of Engineering may specify a minimum performance standard to ensure a
                     sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and

                                                                                                    January 18, 2021
                                                                                                        Page 3 of 30


                iii. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in
                     operation and the Strata Council may not prevent an owner, occupant, or tenant from
                     installing the EV charging equipment.

3.   That the applicant provides more substantial landscaping to better screen the parking located in front
     of the building to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning at the time of Development Permit.

4.   The applicant make a contribution of $75,000 to the City for use towards on-street parking improvement
     on Jenkins Avenue and Avrill Road, prior to the issuance of a Development Variance Permit.

Council has directed Staff to complete the following amendments within Zoning Bylaw No. 300:
        1. To re-organize and simplify the density section of the RM7A Zone;
        2. To allow 918 and 924 Jenkins Avenue to have a FAR of 2.02 within the RM7A Zone;
        3. To amend Schedule AE to include 918 and 924 Jenkins Avenue.

Council has authorized the Director of Planning to issue the following variances through the Development
Permit application:
        1. A parking variance to allow the Mixed Use Employment apartment parking ratio of 1.25 spaces
            per one and two bedroom units, and 2.25 spaces per 3+ bedroom units, to be applied;
        2. An interior side lot line setback variance of 1.4 m instead of the required 3 m; and
        3. A rear setback variance of 6.46 m instead of the required 7.5 m;

Council has directed Staff to provide notice that Council will consider issuance of a Development Variance
Permit for the properties at 918 and 924 Jenkins Avenue for the following variances:
        1. That Section 3.21.02(3) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be waived for the interior side lot line between
            918 and 924 Jenkins Avenue to allow them to opt out of installing a fence and landscape
            screening between the two properties, and;
        2. That Section 3.21(02)(3) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied to reduce the required landscape
             planting area from 1 m to 0.35 m for the properties at 918 and 924 Jenkins, subject to the
            following condition:

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

None presented.

None presented.

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1903 at 5:42 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Ironclad Developments has applied on behalf of the
property owners to rezone 1020 Costin and 2836, 2842, 2848 and 2854 Carlow Road from the 'One- and
Two-Family Residential' zone to the 'City Centre 1' zone to allow for the construction of two 11-storey
residential buildings with a total of 165 units.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

     i. $2,850 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
     ii. $750 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Fund

subject to permitted reductions in accordance with the Affordable Housing and General Amenity
Contribution Policy.

The applicant also agrees to provide the following prior to adoption:

       i. Road dedication to the City, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
      ii. A consolidation plan of the subject properties; and
     iii. A Section 219 covenant registered on title that agrees to the following:

a)     To install all required frontage improvements, recommendations from the Traffic Impact Study, and
       servicing improvements, all to Bylaw No. 1000 standard and prior to issuance of a building permit, to
       the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;

b)     To provide a storm water management plan and install all recommended infrastructure, to the
       satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;


c)     To provide a construction parking management plan prior to the issuance of a building permit, to the

                i.      Detailed renderings, elevations, floor plans and a site plan of the proposed
                        development that clearly illustrates the proposal, all of which complies with the CC1
                        zone; and
               ii.      A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                        managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director
                        of Engineering;

        d) That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in

                i.      That the site be developed with a maximum height limit along the Fairway Avenue

                        of six storeys.

                        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of a building permit;
               iii.     That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for
                        the proposed residential building(s) that ensures parking is allocated to each unit
                        and visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in exchange for
                        compensation separate from that of a residential unit;
               iv.      That no occupancy permit be issued for the proposed building until a strata plan for
                        the building has been registered, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer;
               v.       That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
                        feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to the

                              i. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;

                           of Engineering; and
                  vii.     That a construction parking management plan be provide prior to the issuance of a
                           building permit, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

          Development Permit for 647 Goldstream Avenue:


             a) That Section 6.57.06(2)(a) be varied to reduce the minimum front lot line setback from the

             d) That staff investigate a "right in right out" traffic flow plan for the building.

3.        PUBLIC HEARING


     a)   BYLAW NO. 1864
          "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 574, (Omnibus No. 52 - Residential Zone Combining),
          Bylaw No. 1864, 2020"

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1846 at 5:49 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Bylaw No. 1864 proposes to amend Zoning Bylaw
No. 300 by reducing all one- and two-family and small lot residential zones into just three types of zones:
small lot, one- and two-family residential, and lakeshore residential.

                                                                                                        July 20^ 2020
                                                                                                           Page 2 of 9




Bylaw No. 1864 proposes the following broad changes to Zoning Bylaw No. 300:
• The consolidation of the Residential Small Lot 1 (RSI), Residential Small Lot 2 (RS2), and Residential
    Small Lot 3 (RS3) zones into a single Residential Small Lot 1 zone, where the principal permitted use is a
    one-family dwelling without a suite on lots as small as 200m2, and a one-family dwelling with a suite on
    lots that are not less than 400m2;
•   The consolidation of the One-Family Residential (Rl), the One-and Two-Family Residential (R2), the One-
    and Two-Family Residential A (R2A), the One-to Five Family Residential (R3), the One- Family Residential
    4 (R4) and Residential Small Lot 4 (RS4) zone into a single One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) zone
    where the minimum lot size for a single-family dwelling with a suite is 400m2 and the minimum lot size
    for a two-family dwelling is 600m2 (subject to certain conditions such as lot width);
•   The creation of a new Residential Lakeshore 1 (RLl) zone which encompasses all residential lots that
    are directly adjacent to Florence, Langford and Glen Lake and holds them to their current zoning with
    respect to land use and density under either One-Family Residential (Rl) zone or the One- and Two-
    Family Residential (R2) and the One-and Two-Family Residential A (R2A) zones;
•   Various amendments to Parts 1, 2, 3 and 4 of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 in order to affect the changes listed
    above;
•   Amending the minimum lot size for a two-family dwelling in the CD12 (South Skirt Mountain) zone to
    bring parity between that zone and the CD3 (Westhills) zone in regards to lot size for a two-family
    residential use;

Advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

None presented.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

None presented.

Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the Public Hearing
for Bylaw No. 1864 closed at 5:51 p.m.

    b)   BYLAW NO. 1915
         "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 593, (979 Walfred Rd), Bylaw No. 1915, 2020''

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1915 at 5:51 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Bruce Crawshaw of Westbrook Consulting
Ltd. has applied on behalf of Joseph Antoine Jean Michel Julien to rezone 979 Walfred Road from One-and
Two Family Residential to Residential Small Lot 1.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a three-lot subdivision.

                                                                                                         July 20^ 2020
                                                                                                            Page 3 of 9




As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.
In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

     1. That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions prior to
          subdivision approval:

               a. $3,960 per lot towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
               b. $660 per lot towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

     2. That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a section 219 covenant, registered in priority

Bylaw No. 1864 proposes the following broad changes to Zoning Bylaw No. 300:
• The consolidation of the Residential Small Lot 1 (RSI), Residential Small Lot 2 (RS2), and Residential
    Small Lot 3 (RS3) zones into a single Residential Small Lot 1 zone, where the principal permitted use is a
    one-family dwelling without a suite on lots as small as 200m2, and a one-family dwelling with a suite on
    lots that are not less than 400m2;
•   The consolidation of the One-Family Residential (Rl), the One-and Two-Family Residential (R2), the One-
    and Two-Family Residential A (R2A), the One-to Five Family Residential (R3), the One- Family Residential
    4 (R4) and Residential Small Lot 4 (RS4) zone into a single One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) zone
    where the minimum lot size for a single-family dwelling with a suite is 400m2 and the minimum lot size
    for a two-family dwelling is 600m2 (subject to certain conditions such as lot width);
•   The creation of a new Residential Lakeshore 1 (RLl) zone which encompasses all residential lots that
    are directly adjacent to Florence, Langford and Glen Lake and holds them to their current zoning with
    respect to land use and density under either One-Family Residential (Rl) zone or the One- and Two-
    Family Residential (R2) and the One-and Two-Family Residential A (R2A) zones;
•   Various amendments to Parts 1, 2, 3 and 4 of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 in order to affect the changes listed
    above;

    bring parity between that zone and the CD3 (Westhills) zone in regards to lot size for a two-family
    residential use;

                   Staff Report (Fire Protection)

                                                                                                         July 20^ 2020
                                                                                                            Page 6 of 9




Conor Corbett from Diamond Head Consulting was the lead contact for the project and presented the
findings of the plan to Council at the July 20^^ Meeting. Some of the highlights of the CWPP are as follows:

             o   The previous work in 2002 to establish an interface Fire Hazard Planning Model in our
                 developments has been effective in lowering the interface risk in Langford (pg. 13)
             o   The overall rating for the City is listed as High, however there is additional work can be done
                 to lower the risk further (pg 51)
             o   There are 27 recommendations, many of which can receive additional funding from UBCM
                 to implement that are now possible with the CWPP completed (pgs. i-iv)
             o   Recommendations include measures to manage forest fuel, provide community education,
                 enhance wildfire response and integrate FireSmart planning further into developments.

In order to qualify for UBCM funding, the CWPP needs to adhere to strict guidelines. As a result, the CWPP
does not specifically address private land which accounts for 49% of Langford. However, the
recommendations of the CWPP for the other classes of properties can be used by City Staff to work with
individual home owners or neighbourhoods to help mitigate the interface threat for private property.

In addition, the report recommends the City forming partnerships with surrounding land owners, specifically
CRD Water and BC Parks to help further reduce the risk from wildfire and both agencies are receptive to
working together on these initiatives.

3.      PUBLIC HEARINGS


       a)   BYLAW NO. 1731
            "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 502, (2955 Irwin Rd), 2017".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1731 at 5:31 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                            Page 2 of 9



The City Planner advised that Duncan Magee with Keycorp Developments has applied to amend the zoning
of 2955 Irwin Road from the RR4 (Rural Residential 4) Zone to the RS3 (Residential Small Lot) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of an 18 lot small lot subdivision that will
include trail and park improvements.

This proposal is consistent with the Hillside and Shoreline policy designation within Langford's Official
Community Plan.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

As a bonus for increased density the applicant has agreed to provide the following in accordance with
Council policy:

$ 6,000 per lot or $3960 per small lot towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;

$1000 per lot or $660 per small lot towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

A resident on Ravensview Drive thanked Council for a job well done on recent infrastructure projects.
Noted that the developer is going to great lengths to make this a good project. Raised concerns about
water on Ravensview Drive, in particular low water problems. The resident asked that this be checked on.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

None presented.

The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1731 closed at 5:36 p.m.

Councillor Seaton arrived at 5:44pnn.


        b)   BYLAW NO. 1736
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 468, (2874 Leigh Rd), 2017".


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1736 at 5:37 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                             Page 3 of 9



The City Planner advised that Carole Hutchinson of Design One — Stevens Interiors has applied on behalf
of Derek Hass to amend the text of the R1 (One- and Two-Family) Zone to allow a secondary suite in an
accessory building at 2874 Leigh Road.


As part of this application, a Public Hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide a Section 219 Covenant registered
in priority of all other charges on title that agrees that:

1.    All frontage improvements, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, be constructed or that
      cash-in-lieu of sidewalks, in an amount to be determined by the Director of Engineering be paid to
      the City, prior to Building Permit issuance.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside and Shoreline designation.


Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy. Staff have received
three letters of support for the application and one letter of concern. These letters have been included
in the Public Hearing package.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.


Resident on Kiwi Road gave okay for project with certain conditions. Concerned that there may be a bigger
garage for the surrounding site. Also concerned of decks, windows and doors facing his yard. Lastly,
concerned about the potential sale and safety of his yard.


Matthew Baldwin provided clarification. Existing house will be a garage with secondary new suite in
location of existing garage.


Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

The owner of the property provided clarification. Secondary suite will be close to the water. New principle
dwelling will be where the garage is now, but will be slightly closer to the neighbouring property. The
owner also clarified window positions and screening in neighbouring yard.

Mayor Young asked for a letter saying that it will be owner occupied.


The owner is committed to share plans with neighbours.


The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1736 closed at 5:49 p.m.

        c)   BYLAW NO. 1740
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 506, (1253 Goldstream Ave), 2017".


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1740 at 5:49 p.m.

                                                                                                                Page 4 of 9



Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Duncan Magee has applied on behalf of 0880712 BC LTD to amend the
zoning of the northerly portion of 1253 Goldstream Avenue from the R1 (One-Family Residential) Zone to
the RS4 (Residential Small Lot 4) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of a five lot subdivision.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1.   $3,960 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund for one new lot;
2.   $660 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund for one new lot;
3.   A Section 219 Covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
         a. Register a Statutory Right of Way along the strata common property access road and through
             a 1.8m wide portion of Proposed Lot 4 along the outer edge of the fish bearing stream SPEA
             boundary, reaching the property to be dedicated to the City as park. The SRW shall contain a
             clause that the City will discharge the SRW once an alternate access has been established;
         b. That a Stormwater Management Plan shall be provided and all required measures
             recommended shall be implemented by the owner as a condition of Subdivision approval, to
             the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
         c. That a Construction Parking Management Plan be provided to the satisfaction of the Director
             of Engineering prior to any alteration of the land.
4.   That the applicant pay cash-in-lieu for frontage improvements to the satisfaction of the Director of
     Engineering prior to subdivision.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside and Shoreline designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

None presented.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

Resident on Goldstream Avenue raised concerns about fill and flooding, asked about park access and
raised concerns on parking, especially with suites.

Matthew Baldwin provided clarification on parking requirements.

                                                                                                                    Page 5 of 9



The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1740 closed at 5:50 p.m.

canonical_motions.agenda_item_title: Bylaw No. 2217 - Application for a Text Amendment to Allow for a School
canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
THAT Council:

                 1. Direct staff to give notice that Council will consider First, Second and Third
                    Reading of Bylaw No. 2217 to amend the text of the BP9 zone to add 'School' as
                    a permitted use for the property located at 691 Kodiak Way subject to the
                    following terms and conditions:

                     a. That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption, registers a Section 219
                        covenant in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the
                        following:

                         i.   That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000
                              standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the
                              issuance of a building permit:

                              1. A storm water management plan; and

                              2. A mitigation plan.

                         ii. That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets
                             or exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets
                             based on Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the
                             issuance of a Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type III
                             Environmental Product Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying
                             the total Global Warming Potential value and confirming that the
                             proposed development meets the requirements of Low Carbon
                             Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN.

            "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 409, (Omnibus No. 39 — Various Amendments),
            2016".

The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1531 at 5:35 p.m.


Acting Mayor Seaton advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or
her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. A/Mayor Seaton advised that after
everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be
heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                         Regular Council Minutes —October 3, 2016
                                                                                                      Page 2 of 8




The City Planner advised that the City of Langford is proposing to make various omnibus amendments to
the City of Langford's Zoning Bylaw No. 300. These amendments include:
     •   generally increasing the maximum height permitted for apartment buildings from four storeys to
         six storeys;
     •   changing the ground floor parking requirements in the C8 (Community Town Centre Pedestrian)
         zone;
     •   adding "apartment" as a permitted use on two properties in the Business and Technology 1 (BT1)
         zone,
     •   rectifying certain legal non-conforming uses;
     •   adjusting the boundary of the CH4 (Cluster Housing 4) zone to include lands that are straddling
         the zoning boundary; and
     •   allowing shipping containers as a permitted accessory use to mini-storage


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act. This proposal is consistent with Official Community Plan Designations. Advertisements
have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Acting Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Acting Mayor Seaton called a second time for presentations.

The Acting Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Acting Mayor
officially declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1531 closed at 5:36 p.m.

 This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of an apartment building at 720 and 724

       a) BYLAW NO. 1681
           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 477, (2762 and 2768 Claude Rd), 2017".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1681 at 5:32 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                   May 15TH, 2017
                                                                                                     Page 2 of 18




The City Planner advised that Matthew McKay, DB Services of Victoria Inc., has applied on behalf of
Matthew and Margaret McKay and Danny Lahnsteiner to amend the zoning of the properties at 2762 and
2768 Claude Rd from the R1 (One-Family Residential) Zone to the MU2 (Mixed-Use Residential
Commercial) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the construction of an eleven (11) storey residential building
consisting of approximately 117 residential dwelling units.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:
         • $1,525 per dwelling unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund, which may be reduced
               to $381.25 per unit if the project is secured as rental housing;
         • $610 per dwelling unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund, which may be reduced
               to $152.50 per unit if the project is secured as rental housing;
         • A Section 219 covenant, prior to Bylaw adoption, which secures the following conditions:
                   o That the owner will pay for and construct all works to restrict left turn movements
                       southbound on Claude Road to Goldstream Avenue prior to issuance of Occupancy
                       Permit;
                   o That the owner will provide a traffic and public safety plan and construction parking
                       management plan, prior to any onsite works and/or clearing, to the satisfaction of
                       the Director of Engineering;
                   o That the owner shall construct frontage improvements, works and services to the
                       standards of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 and to the
