       a)   BYLAW NO. 1748
            "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 514, (2844 Millstream Rd), 2017".


The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1748 at 5:32 p.m.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or
her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that after

                                                                                                      January 8th, 2018
                                                                                                           Page 2 of 16


everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be
heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Pascal Toupin- Selinger with Ironclad Developments has applied on behalf
of Andre Louis Cottyn to amend the zoning of 2844 Millstream Rd from the CS1 (Service Commercial) Zone
to the MUlA (Mixed Use Residential Commercial A) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to include the subject parcel in plans to construct an apartment building
on 720, 724 and 732 Meaford Avenue.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:


1.   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
     unit, which may be reduced by 75% if rental tenure is secured for a term of no less than 10 years, prior
     to subdivision approval:


     a)     $2,562 per unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
     b)     $610 per unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority of all
other charges on title, that agrees to the following:


           i.That the applicant provide a construction parking management plan, to the satisfaction of the
              Director of Engineering, prior to issuance of a building permit;
           ii.That the applicant provide a stormwater management plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of
              Engineering and in accordance with Bylaw No. 1000, prior to subdivision approval or building
              permit issuance, whichever is first;
          iii.That the applicant acknowledges and agrees to design the proposed development, in accordance
              to the updated parking regulations as determined by Council, to the discretion of the Director of
              Planning;
          iv.That the applicant agrees to implement the approved storm water management plan and to
              complete any required improvements and/or upgrades to on site and off site infrastructure
          necessary to facilitate proper drainage on the subject property at the applicant's expense;
       v.That the applicant will construct full frontage improvements, including, but not limited to, the
          installation of a sidewalk to the corner of Meaford and Millstream Road to align with the sidewalk
          infrastructure required along Meaford Road, in accordance with Bylaw No.1000 and to the
          satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to subdivision approval or building permit
          issuance, whichever is first;
      vi.That any necessary above or underground infrastructure or servicing upgrades, extensions or
          other required servicing requirements are to be fulfilled at the applicant's expense; and
      vii.That the applicant acknowledges the proximity to industrial business operators may be a nuisance
          to the future residents of the development;


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

                                                                                                      January 8th, 2018
                                                                                                          Page 3 of 16


Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Acting Mayor called a first time for presentations.

None presented.

The Acting Mayor called a second time for presentations.

None presented.

The Acting Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Acting Mayor officially
declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1748 closed at 5:34 p.m.

             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 516, (798 Goldstream Ave; 2747, 2753, 2761, 2769
             & 2779 Peatt Rd; 2734, 2738, 2742, 2746, 2750 & 2756 Claude Rd), 2017".

The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1750 at 5:34 p.m.

Acting Mayor Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his
or her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that after
everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be
heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Niall Paltiel of Island View Strategies has applied on behalf of Bishop of
Victoria Corporation (Our Lady of Rosary Catholic Church) to amend the zoning of 2747, 2753, 2761, 2769,
and 2779 Peatt Road; 2734, 2738, 2742, 2746, 2750, and 2756 Claude Road; and 798 Goldstream Avenue
from the P2 (Community Institutional), R1 (One-Family Residential), R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential)
Zone to a new C9 (Community Town Centre Pedestrian 9) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for a future mixed-used development on these properties
along with a new church and parish location.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1.
     a.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
           residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:
                i.     $1,525 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                       $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund.

                                                                                                     January 8th, 2018
                                                                                                          Page 4 of 16


Unless Council amends the Amenity Contribution policy prior to second reading of Bylaw No. 1750 in
which case the applicant may request that Council amend Bylaw No. 1750 to include the contribution
amounts.

     b.    That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
           square metre of commercial space, prior to issuance of a building permit:
                i.   $10.75 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.


     c.    That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the following:
                i.    A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                      managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director
                      of Engineering.
                      The registration of a lot consolidation plan that includes road dedication along Peatt
                      Road, Goldstream Avenue, and Claude Road to the satisfaction of the Manager of
                      Land Development and Director of Engineering;
                      The registration a blanket statutory right of way on the proposed church/assisted
                      living site for a pedestrian connection between Peatt Road and Claude Road; and
               iv.    The registration of a blanket statutory right of way on the southwest site for the
                      future installation of a pedestrian friendly plaza in the southwest corner, which would
                      include art work.
     d.   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered in priority
          of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:
                 i.   That a 2.0m wide pedestrian connection between Peatt Road and Claude Road be
                      constructed with red brick paves and lighting prior to issuance of a building permit,
                      to the satisfaction of the Parks Manager; and
                      That the southwest corner of the proposed commercial/residential site have a 300m2
                      pedestrian plaza with art work installed prior to issuance of a building permit, to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Planning;
                      That a Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) be completed to the satisfaction of the
                      Director of Engineering for the full build-out of any block that commercial and/or
                      residential uses are proposed, prior to the issuance of building permit, and that the
                      recommendations of the TIA be implemented;
               iv.    That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of a building permit; and
                v.    That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building
                      permit and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of
                      Engineering;


2.   Direct staff to enter into a shared parking agreement with owner(s) of the future church property
     that allows them exclusive privilege to the Danbrook parking lot on Sunday mornings and religions
     holidays in exchange for parking privileges of their private parking lot for the general public during
     daytime hours Monday to Friday, excluding religious holidays.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

                                                                                                     January 8th, 2018
                                                                                                         Page 5 of 16

The Acting Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Resident on Green Mansions Place, Langford (Owns property that is adjacent) — Addressed Council with
concerns that the proposal is open ended. Would like to see more information on old and new housing
(site lines, traffic flow). The resident equated the proposal to signing a blank cheque. Also concerned
about the limit potential for solar panels on his roof, about removal of existing housing and where the
current folks will live and about the vastness of the proposal.

The Acting Mayor called a second time for presentations.

None presented.

The Acting Mayor called a third time for presentations.

Same resident raised concerns about existing renters and where they would live.

Jim Hartshorne (developer) — provided input, the Catholic Church subsidizes rentals.

Resident asked about public parking.

Matthew Baldwin (City Planner) — provided clarification to reciprocal agreement, as did Jim Hartshorne.

Another resident — raised concerns about notification and timing.

Niall Paltiel (developer) — Provided clarification and will give as much notice as possible. He also provided
clarification on behalf of the applicant.

There being no more presentations, the Acting Mayor officially declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No.
1750 closed at 5:57 p.m.

canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
That the City of Langford, in order to ensure value for money, appropriate scope of work, no
       duplication between the various levels of government, and no shifting of the capital costs of
       transportation infrastructure onto the Capital Regional District, requests that the Capital Regional
       District provide all municipalities and electoral areas within the regional district with detailed
       information on the funding amount required by the Regional Transportation Service
       Establishment Bylaw for the next five years and what it will be used for;


       AND


       That the City of Langford does not support a Capital Regional District Regional Transportation
       Service that does not allow each municipality and electoral area within the regional district time
       to review the detailed information on the required funding amounts and objectives, and to opt
       out of the Regional Transportation Service if it so wishes;

       AND


       That, in this instance, the City of Langford does not support an Alternate Approval Process to
       obtain approval from municipal electors for the Regional Transportation Service, but believes
       consent should be provided in accordance with s. 346 of the Local Government Act, whereby
       consent is provided by each municipal Council (consenting on behalf of municipal electors) and
       by Alternative Approval Process in each Electoral Area.

       AND


       That the City of Langford reaffirms its support for a no-cost advisory committee made of local
       government representatives to provide recommendations and priorities to BC Transit and the
       Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure

canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
That Council:

1.   Give 1st reading to the Bylaw No. 1749 to amend the zoning designation of the property located at 790
     McCallum from CH1 (Cluster Housing Residential) to a new MUE2 (Mixed-Use Employment 2) Zone with
     the addition of a three-storey height limit on townhouses and subject to the following terms and
     conditions:
            a) That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contribution
                 prior to issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval:

                     i.    The dedication of 16,200m2 of land in a block form and location to the satisfaction
                           of the Director of Planning; and
                    ii.    $1,000,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund for this site;
                           OR
                    iii.   An amenity building on this site to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning,
                           with a certified construction value of $1,000,000; and
                    iv.    $500,000 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund for this site;
                           OR
                    v.     Arts and Cultural structure(s) on this site to the satisfaction of the Director of
                           Planning with a certified construction value of $500,000.

              b)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the following:

                     i.    A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                           managed on-site for the proposed development, to the satisfaction of the
                           Director of Engineering.
                    ii     The registration a 10m wide statutory right of way along the western and
                           southern edges of the property for trail purposes; and
                   iii.    Road dedication at Treanor Avenue for the future construction of a roundabout
                           to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

              c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
                   in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

                                                                                                      January 8th, 2018
                                                                                                         Page 15 of 16


                   I.    That a four-way signalized intersection be installed on McCallum Road at the
                         main entry point to Costco (easterly) prior to issuance of a building permit or
                         subdivision approval;
                   ii.   That a roundabout be constructed along the frontage of this property on
                         Treanor Road prior to issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, to
                         the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.
                  iii.   That a landscaped and irrigated trail be constructed along the southern and
                         western edges within the 10m wide statutory right of way to bylaw 1000
                         standards prior to issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, and to
                         the satisfaction of the Manager of Parks;
                  iv.    That all road dedication including widening of McCallum Road and any new
                         internal municipal road is provided prior to issuance of a building permit or
                         subdivision approval to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and
                         Approving Officer;
                  v.     That a Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) be completed prior to issuance of a
                         building permit or subdivision approval to the satisfaction of the Director of
                         Engineering for the proposed development, and that the recommendations of
                         the TIA be implemented;
                  vi.    That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided prior to
                         issuance of a building permit or subdivision approval, to the satisfaction of the
                         Director of Engineering; and
                 vii.    That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building
                         permit or subdivision approval and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the
                         satisfaction of the Director of Engineering; AND

2.   Direct staff to release the existing 30m wide restrictive covenant in exchange for of a 10m wide statutory
     right of way for a buffer and trail.

4.      PUBLIC PARTICIPATION


Resident on Kingswood Rd - In regards to 494 Goldstream (item 5a), there was no notification to residents on
Kristina Place and Kingswood Road for the Goldstream proposal. No one in the neighbourhood is in favour.

L. Stohmann, Deputy Director of Planning - Notification happens before the public hearing, so the report on
the Council agenda is an initial introduction and public notification will take place later in the process.

Second resident on Kingswood Rd - 494 Goldstream Avenue property has some very large trees, and is home
to many animals. Traffic on Goldstream and neighbouring streets will increase. Suggest that a smaller building
would be more appropriate for the neighbourhood - 2 to 3 stories instead of 5 to 6.

Representative for owner of 494 Goldstream - Owner would like to keep it freehold, not strata due to cost of
strata conversion.


Third resident on Kingswood Rd - The 494 Goldstream project will cause parking concerns and safety issues for
neighbourhood children.

L. Stohmann. Deputv Director of Planning -There is no variance requested for parking; the project is currently
proposing to include all required parking on site.

canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
That Council direct staff to bring forward an additional report outlining the extent of the
        requested variances and a bylaw to amend the zoning designation of the property located at 494
        Goldstream Avenue from R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) to CCl (CityCentre) subject to the
        following terms and conditions:

        a) That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per
            residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:

                i.      $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund;
               ii.      $2,850 toward the General Amenity Fund; and

        subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the Affordable Housing
        and Amenity Contribution Policy.

              iii.      $10.75 per m2 of commercial Gross Floor Area.

        b) That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:

                                                                                                       June 8th, 2020
                                                                                                          Page 3 of 8



             i.    A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                   managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director of
                   Engineering.

      c) That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a section 219 covenant, registered in
         priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

             i.    That all frontage improvements along Goldstream Avenue and Kristina Place are
                   provided as per Bylaw 1000, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering, prior to
                   the issuance of a Building Permit;
            ii.    That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building permit
                   and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of
                   Engineering;
            iii.   That a construction parking and traffic management plan be provided prior to the
                   issuance of a building permit, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
            iv.    That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the
                   proposed residential building that ensures parking is assigned and tied to each unit
                   created in accordance with the minimum required parking stalls as per the zoning
                   bylaw.
             v.    That no occupancy permit be issued for the proposed building until a strata plan for the
                   building has been registered, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer.

3.       PUBLIC HEARINGS

         a) BYLAW NO. 1608
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 444, (Omnibus No. 43 —Various Amendments to
             General Regulations), 201511 .

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1608 at 7:03 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The Acting City Planner advised the City of Langford is proposing to make various omnibus amendments
to the City of Langford's Zoning Bylaw No. 300t h and that the purpose of the Public Hearing was to hear
from the public regarding Bylaw No. 1608 which, if adopted, would amend the following:

     •   General regulations relating to Home Occupation;
     •   Permitted projections into required setbacks;
     •   Maximum fence height;
     •   Changing the "office" permitted use in the P1B Zone to accessory only;
     •   Allowing secondary suites in the RS4 Zone on lots greater than or equal to 400 m2; and
     •   Differentiating between cardlock gasoline stations and retail gasoline stations.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act. This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan designations and
notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1608 closed at 7:05 p.m.

their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that Seamus Brennan of Keycorp Consulting Ltd. has applied on behalf of
Oakcrest Park Estates Ltd., Raymond Mew, Gilbert Chew, Wai Yuen, Ronald Kenneth Westwood, Mew
Properties, 429176 BC Ltd., Roberta Hilda Young and Ridley Bros Development Co. Ltd. to amend the
Official Community Plan designation of the commonly referred 'Centre Mountain Properties' to Business
or Light Industrial and Hillside or Shoreline and to amend the zoning of the commonly referred 'Centre
Mountain Properties' to the BP8 (Business Park 8), RR4 (Rural Residential 4) and CH5 (Cluster Housing
5)Zones.

This is being proposed to permit the rezoning of these lands for Business Park and residential uses and to
bring lands formerly within the District of Metchosin under City of Langford zoning.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

The City is also proposing to amend the City of Langford Official Community Plan to include those lands
recently added to the City of Langford from the District of Metchosin and to update various maps within
the OCP accordingly. The rezoning proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Business or
Light Industrial and Hillside or Shoreline designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

The Mayor called a third and final time for presentations.

A Metchosin Resident approached Council with concern regarding traffic access off of Happy Valley Road.

A citizen residing at 3031 Sooke Road addressed Council in regards to the neighbouring business park and
would like to see a green space retained.

A citizen residing on Summer Breeze Lane addressed Council requesting a buffer between his property
and the new area, and asked for a road access to be through the industrial park instead of off of Happy
Valley Road.

3.     PUBLIC HEARINGS


        a)   BYLAW NO. 1717
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 507, (2500 Echo Valley Dr), 2017".


The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1717 at 5:32 p.m.

Acting Mayor M. Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that
his or her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the
matters contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw
should give their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. The Acting Mayor advised that
after everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to
be heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                           March 19th, 2018
                                                                                               Page 2 of 14



The City Planner advised that Rachael Sansom of Turner Lane Development Corp. has applied on
behalf of 1085540 BC Ltd. to amend the text of "Area 2" in the CD6 (Comprehensive Development
6 — Bear Mountain) Zone to allow for a townhouse development at 2500 Echo Valley Drive.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the
Local Government Act. In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the
following items prior to Public Hearing:


1. A detailed site plan illustrating two routes for access to and egress from the site;
2. A stormwater management plan; and
3.   Confirmation of adequate water, fire flow and sanitary sewer capacities to serve the
      proposed development; and


The applicant has submitted the required access plan, and a Servicing Feasibility Study to the
satisfaction of the Director of Engineering (it should be noted that the study has been approved
for conceptual stormwater management only, all other servicing is subject to detailed design
approval. Detailed stormwater calculations will be required during site servicing and will be
subject to further approvals by the City).


The applicant has also agreed to provide a Section 219 Covenant, prior to Bylaw Adoption,
addressing frontage improvements, stormwater management, water supply, road access to
adjacent properties, local service agreements and firefighting provisions.


This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Hillside or Shoreline designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.


Concurrent with this application, Council may also wish to consider discharging a Covenant
registered as a condition of rezoning for the properties located at 1410 Grand Forest Close, 1431
Grand Forest Close and 2342 Lairds Gate which are adjacent to the subject property.                  This
Covenant was registered at the request of the previous owner of 2500 Echo Valley Drive in order
to restrict development of these adjacent properties to minimize the potential impact of
development on the property at 2500 Echo Valley Drive.


Ownership of 2500 Echo Valley has since changed, and the new owner wishes to develop the
property as evidenced by this application. Council may therefore wish to discharge the Covenant
on 1410 Grand Forest Close, 1431 Grand Forest Close and 2342 Lairds Gate in advance of the 5
year timeline expiry date.

The Acting Mayor called a first time for presentations.

None presented.

Acting Mayor called a second time for presentations.

                                                                                                 March 19th, 2018
                                                                                                     Page 3 of 14


None presented.


The Acting Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Acting Mayor
officially declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1717 closed at 5:35 p.m.

        b)   BYLAW NO.'s 1737 and 1742
             "Langford Official Community Plan Bylaw, Amendment No. 26, (2869 Sooke Rd —Road
             Closure Portion), 2018".
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 509, (2869 Sooke Rd Portion), 2018".


The Acting Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1737 and 1742 at 5:36 p.m.

Acting Mayor M. Sahlstrom advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that
his or her interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the
matters contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw
should give their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Acting Mayor M. Sahlstrom
advised that after everyone has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else
who wishes to be heard", and if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared
closed.

The City Planner advised that Mr. Richard Irwin applied on behalf of 89 Chicken Ranch Ltd to amend the
zoning of 3370, 3344 Luxton Road and 2869 Sooke Road from the from RR2 (Rural Residential 2) Zone to
Business Park 2A — Sooke Road West (BP2A) Zone, the Bylaw associated with this amendment was
adopted by Council at their December 8th, 2017 meeting.


A condition of this Zoning amendment was the closure of Luxton Road between Marwood Avenue and
Sooke Road. In order to facilitate traffic flow along the new extension of Marwood Avenue that would
connect to Sooke Road through the subject property.


The portion of Luxton Road will stay open until the new road is fully operational, however, the developer
would like to amend this portion of road so as it can be integrated into the development plans of the
adjacent parcel once the road is closed.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.


The Acting Mayor called a first time for presentations.


None presented.


Acting Mayor M. Sahlstrom called a second time for presentations.


Resident on Regal Court spoke about traffic concerns.


Director Michelle Mahovlich provided clarification regarding the new Marwood and Sooke Road signal

                                                                                                 March 19th, 2018
                                                                                                     Page 4 of 14



intersection.


Resident on Regal Court asked about the crosswalk on Penwood Road.

Director Michelle Mahovlich confirmed that it would be integrated into the new signal.


Resident on Luxton Road asked about increased traffic and the elementary school.


Resident on Regal Court asked about sewers on Marwood Road.


Director Michelle Mahovlich provided background and offered follow up.


The Acting Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Acting Mayor
officially declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1737 and 1742 closed at 5:42 p.m.

6.      DEVELOPMENT VARIANCE PERMIT


         a)   DVP17-0023 — 2579 Rainville Rd

canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
That Development Variance Permit No. DVP17-0023 be issued by the Council for the City of Langford
to Dan Hodge on behalf of Dan and Munirih Hodge to reduce the minimum rear yard setback from 6.0 m
(20 ft) to 2.7 m (9 ft) and defer the requirement for the installation of on-site plumbing to allow for the
construction of an addition to the existing one-family dwelling at 2579 Rainville Road subject to the
following terms and conditions:



1.   Appendix


     The site shall be developed in accordance with the site plan attached (Appendix A).

                                                                                                  March 19th, 2018
                                                                                                      Page 6 of 14




2.    Variances


      The following regulations of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 are varied under Section 498 of the Local
      Government Act:

      a)   That Section 6.21.06(1)(a) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied to reduce the minimum setback from
           the rear lot line from 6.0 m (20 ft) to 2.7 m (9 ft); and
      b)   That Section 6.1.2(c) of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to defer
           the installation of on-site plumbing from prior to the issuance of an Occupancy Permit for the
           proposed addition to within six months of a sewer main being installed in a highway or City
           statutory right-of-way abutting the property at 2579 Rainville Road;

3.    Conditions

      The following requirements are imposed under Section 498 of the Local Government Act:


      I.  That the site is developed in substantial accordance with the plans attached to this report as
          Appendix C;
      II. That the owner registers a Section 219 Covenant, in priority of all other charges, prior to the
          issuance of this Development Variance Permit that agrees that all required on-site plumbing will
          be installed and connected to the municipal sanitary sewer system within six months of a sewer
          main being installed in a highway or City statutory right-of-way abutting the parcel;
     III. That the owner pays the required Sewer Capital Recovery Fee (SCRF) to West Shore
          Environmental Services or the City of Langford prior to the issuance of a Building Permit
          authorizing the construction of the proposed addition at 2579 Rainville Road; and
     IV. That the owner provides confirmation of adequate septic field capacity for the proposed
          addition containing a shop and secondary suite from Island Health prior to the issuance of a
          Building Permit authorizing the construction of the proposed addition at 2579 Rainville Road.

canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
That Council:

                                                                                                March 19th, 2018
                                                                                                    Page 7 of 14




1.   Give 1st reading to the attached Bylaw No. 1767 to amend the zoning designation of the properties
     located at 2682, 2684, 2686, 2696, 2702, and 2706 Sooke Road from District Commercial (C3) and
     Service Commercial (CS1) to a new Community Town Centre Pedestrian 9 (C9) zone subject to the
     following terms and conditions:


         a)   That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions
              per residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:

                 i.   $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund, and either
                 ii. $2,074 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund, OR
                 iii. Full road improvements for the realignment of Glen Lake Road


         b) That the applicant provides, prior to public hearing, the following:

                 i.    A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately
                       managed for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director of
                       Engineering.


         c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
              in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

                 i.    That the owner will not apply for, nor is the City obligated to issue a Development
                       Permit, Building Permit, or Subdivision until the road (as shown) has been
                       dedicated.
                ii.    That at any time after the 5th anniversary date of adoption of the bylaw to rezone
                       the subject lands, that the City may request, and the owner shall provide, the area
                       of land necessary for the construction of the road extension from Happy Valley
                       Road to Glen Lake Road as well as Sooke Road for $1.00.
                iii.   That the owner will limit direct vehicular access to Sooke Road, and will not apply
                       for, nor will the City be obligated to grant driveway access on to Sooke Road,
                       except in accordance with a comprehensive plan of development for the
                       properties as a whole.
                iv.    That the owner will provide an easement for reciprocal vehicular access in
                       conjunction with any Development Permit where various properties may be
                       affected, to the satisfaction of the City Planner.
                v.     That a Traffic Impact Assessment (TIA) be completed to the satisfaction of the
                       Director of Engineering for the full build-out of any block that commercial and/or
                       residential uses are proposed, prior to the issuance of building permit, and that
                       the recommendations of the TIA be implemented prior to Occupancy of any
                       buildings;
               vi.     That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided to the
                       satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and Manager of Parks prior to issuance
                       of a building permit; and
               vii.    That a detailed storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a
                       building permit and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the
                       Director of Engineering.

                                                                                                    March 19th, 2018
                                                                                                        Page 8 of 14


   2.   Direct the City Planner to permit onsite parking, through the Development Permit for Form and
        Character, to be at a ratio of 1.0 stall per 1 or 2 bedroom units, with any additional 0.25 for visitor
        parking.


   3.   Direct the City Planner to permit onsite parking and loading facilities, through the Development
        Permit for Form and Character, to be located in the front or side yards for buildings located
        immediately next to the Galloping Goose.

        to the Neighbourhood Institutional (PIA) Zone, and to amend the text of the PIA zone

        In support ofthis application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following prior to

        a. $6,000.00 for a sidewalk on the Sooke Rd. frontage ofthestrata property, to the
        satisfaction of the Directorof Engineering.

        This proposal is consistent with the current Official Community Plan "Neighbourhood
        Centre" designation

        Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
        Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations. None.


Mayor Young called a second time for presentations. None.

Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the

3.2     BYLAW NO. 1856

       The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1856 at 5:35 pm.
        Deputy Director of Planning Leah Stohmann advised that Rachael Sansom has applied
       on behalfof 1177016 BC Ltd. to amend the zoning of 2627 and 2631 Millstream Road
       from the R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential Zone to the RM9 (Medium Density
       Apartment) Zone.

       This is being proposed in order to allow for the development ofan apartment building
       with approximately 113 units.

       As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the
       regulations of the Local Government Act.

       In support ofthis application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:
       a) As a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per residential unit,
       prior to issuance of a building permit:

i. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund;
ii. $3,660 towards the General Annenity Reserve Fund;
iii. (i) and (ii) are subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance
with the Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy;
iv. That the total amount of contribution, after reductions, to the General Amenity
Reserve Fund may be reduced by the estimated cost of installing additional sidewalk in
front of the properties located at 2635 Millstream Road and 2623-2579 Millstream
Road, as well as the cost of installing a flashing pedestrian crossing, to the satisfaction of
the Director of Engineering;

b) That, prior to BylawAdoption, the developer:

1.    Provides a Section 219 covenant registered in priority of all other charges on title
that agrees to the following:

1. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards
to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior the issuance of a building permit:

a. Full frontage improvements, including the installation of sidewalks along the
frontage of the properties and along the frontage of 2635 Millstream Road and 2623-
2579 Millstream Road, as well as the installation of a flashing pedestrian crossing.
b.     A storm water management plan;
c.    A construction parking management plan

2. That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades required to the
services and utilities required for the development;


3. That the developer registers a strata plan, prior to the issuance of an occupancy
permit, that creates individual strata titles for each resident unit;


4. That the developer consolidates the properties prior to the issuance of a
development permit;



5. That the required parking stalls for this development are allocated for the use by
 individuals in each unit and visitors, as required by Bylaw No. 300, and that parking is
not separated from individual units nor provided in exchange for compensation
separate than that of the residential unit; and
 a.    That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to the
parking space; and
 b.    Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging; and

        c. Where an electric vehicle energy nnanagement system is implemented (load
        sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard to
        ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
        d. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in
        operation and the Strata Council may not preventan owner, occupant, or tenant from
        installing the EV charging equipment.

        This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood
        designation.

        Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
        Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.


        Rachael Sansom, 1498 White Pine Terrace - The applicant has addressed concerns
        though larger setbacks, sidewalks, and flashing pedestrian crossing. The density allows
        for more families in a smaller area.



        Marguerite Coady, 682 Charmar Cres - Appreciate the new sidewalks. Request
        neighbourhood parking designation rather than City Centre parking.


       Jessie Priest, 2849 Lake End Rd - Support this project. We need more housing, support
        building up not out.


       Amber Baker, 2670Winster Rd - Supportdevelopment. Pleased there will be sufficient
       parking, support the proposed light-controlled crossing.


       Dana Elizabeth, 2850Aldwynd Rd - Supportthis application, we need more affordable
       housing options. Support EV charging and crosswalks.


       Kevin Jones, 472 Regency PI - Support this, we need more affordable housing.

       Lane Britton, 3022 Shoreview Dr - Support this, this is an opportunity for affordable
       housing.


       Laurie Plomp, 3592 Whimfield Terr-Meeting ID number was incorrect on Friday, will
       Council consider postponing the hearing.

            Marie Watmough, Acting Director of Corporate Services - The correct number was
            posted on Saturday and the notices were correct.


            Tony Zarskias, 3645 Tillicum Rd - Calling in to represent a Langford business. It's
            important to build up, not out.


            Albert Internicola, 670 Marlisa PI - It's people who don't live in the neighbourhood who
            support this. Neighbourhood can't support 113 more vehicles. Do not support.


            Ron Bain, 719 Massie Dr - Do not support, roads are already at maximum capacity.


     Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.


            Tom Miller, 661 Marlisa PI - Do not support, the proposed development is too tall.
            Other people calling in don't understand that the neighbourhood is already dense.


            Albert Internicola, 670 Marlisa PI - Building will shadow neighbourhood, would support
            a smaller building.



            Jacqueline Gintaut, 1331 Ravensview Dr - A number of issues with this development
            that were brought up earlier have not been addressed. If approved, the parking
            designation should be Neighbourhood and not City Centre.


     Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the
     Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1856 closed at 6:02 p.m.

canonical_motions.agenda_item_title: Application to Rezone 2633 to 2647 Sunderland Road, 808 to 820 Arncote, and
canonical_motions.source_motion_text:
That Council:



       1. Direct staff to prepare a bylaw to amend the zoning designation of the
       properties located at 2633, 2637, 2641, and 2647 Sunderland Road, 808, 812,
       and 820 Arncote, and 2630, 2636, 2640, and 2646 Peatt Road from the R2 (One-
       and Two-Family Residential) zone to the CCP (City Centre Pedestrian) zone
       subject to the following terms and conditions:

       a) That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
       contributions per residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:
       i. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Fund; and
        ii. $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund
       subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the
       Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.
        b) That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following
        contributions per square metre of commercial space, prior to issuance of a
        building permit:
        i. $10.75 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund.
        c) That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following to the
        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering:
        i. A technical memo from a qualified engineer that verifies stormwater can be
        adequately managed on-site for the proposed developments;
        ii. A revised ground floor plan be submitted that complies with City Centre
        Pedestrian zone, to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning;
        iii. A Traffic Impact Assessment from a qualified engineer be provided
        regarding the proposed development.
        iv. Civil drawings that illustrate the additional road improvements outlined in
        the Traffic Impact Study, including an outline of any additional land required to
        complete these works.
        V.   That the applicant provide new drawings that show ground floor
        commercial uses and greenspace on-site.
        d)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219
        covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the
        following:

         i. That ail 11 properties associated with this rezoning be consolidated together
         prior to issuance of a Development Permit for Form and Character;
        ii. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance ofa building permit
        for the proposed residential building(s) that ensures parking is allocated to each
        unit and visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in
        exchange for compensation separate from that of a residential unit;
        iii. That no occupancy permit be issued for the proposed building until a strata
        plan for the building has been registered, to the satisfaction ofthe Approving
        Officer;

        iv. That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces,
        shall feature an energized outletcapable of providing Level 2 charging or higher
        to the parking space, and that
        1. Energized outletsshall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
        2. Where an electric vehicle energy management system is implemented (load
        sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance standard
        to ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and
        3. The owner/tenant is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing
        Equipment (EVSE) in operation and the Strata Council/landlord may not prevent
        an owner, occupant, or tenant from installing the EV charging equipment
        V. That the following are implemented to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
        satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to issuance of a building permit:
        1.   Frontage improvements on all three roads, and all recommended
        improvements from the Traffic Impact Assessment, which may include land
        acquisition at the applicant's expense along Peatt Road;
        2.   Formalize improvements to the pedestrian connection north of the site;
        3.   A storm water management plan; and
        4.   A construction parking management plan.

canonical_motions.seconder: THAT Council approve the following expenditures from the funds allocated in the budget for initiatives arising from the Community Safety Working Groups: Authorize the hiring of one additional RCMP officer at an annual cost of $225,000 Creation of a small business grant program in the amount of $50,000 to be administered by the West Shore Chamber of Commerce for security improvements Authorize the addition of one full-time equivalent bike patrol officer Authorize staff to enter into a service agreement with the Salvation Army for up to $50,000 for the purpose of providing space where members of the community can connect with social services and other supports to mitigate and prevent homelessness. AND THAT Council direct staff as follows: Create a program wherein the Fire Department and RCMP visit small businesses to review their layout and make recommendations to minimize risks of theft while still ensuring the exits are clear and accessible in the event of an emergency. Work with the RCMP to facilitate coordination meetings of Loss Prevention Officers. Prepare and initiate a community campaign, together with the RCMP, encouraging block and neighbourhood watch programs. Work with the Building Officials Association and developers to ensure crime prevention measures are included in the design of new housing. Work with the development community to protect construction sites and equipment through theft prevention programs such as tool marking and identification. Explore options for broad public communication around property crime prevention ideas as well as reporting out on enforcement activities and outcomes to enhance public awareness and preparedness. Draft a bylaw for consideration at a future Council meeting that places restrictions on the purchase and sale of spray paint and bear spray and requiring that these sprays be locked up rather than freely available. Work on a robust public awareness and personal safety education campaign with respect to park and trail safety and a coordinated use of social media and other communication channels to encourage active use of parks and trails and remind people of their obligations with respect to having dogs in parks and on trails. Explore options for CRD Bylaw officers to join the City’s bylaw officers in undertaking joint patrols and hosting joint information sessions in parks and on trails, and for the City and CRD to actively engage with the School District and community partner organizations to expand free and accessible recreational, educational, and stewardship programming in City parks and trails. Ensure all Bylaw Enforcement employees and Fire Fighters receive trauma-informed training and that the City encourage CRD Bylaw Enforcement employees to also participate in the training, either as part of the City’s group or on their own. Review all of the City’s policies and practices to ensure that they are in alignment with human rights commission findings, federal housing policies and recent legal decisions. Facilitate semi-annual meetings of the working group meetings to allow them to come together to discuss issues in a less formal, supportive environment. AND THAT Council further direct staff to send letters to the CRD and the Province advocating for the following: The CPOII program be fully funded through the Province, with an eye to expand. The Province allocate ongoing funding to create a support resource to help those in need navigate a complex system to find appropriate services; to allocate additional spending on health and addiction services and improved disability and other social programs; and to establish a guaranteed minimum income. The CRD continue to improve the regional trail network with additional lighting, trail paving, and CEPTED design considerations for those portions of the regional trails within the West Shore. AND THAT Council work towards permanent solutions, in conjunction with our West Shore neighbours, to seek a seat at the Region’s Homelessness Encampment Working Group Response Leadership Table advocating to the Province for more varied social housing types, especially transitional housing. AND THAT Council direct staff to bring back a draft Community Safety Plan for consideration before December 31, 2026.

canonical_motions.source_motion_text: THAT Council: 1.    Consider bringing forward Bylaw No. 2290 for first, second and third readings at a future Council meeting in order to amend the zoning designation of the properties located at 2639 and 2645 Sooke Road from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) Zone to the Mixed Use Six Storey (MU6) Zone, subject to the following terms and conditions: a.    That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption , registers a road dedication plan to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and Public Works; b.    That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption , registers a Section 219 covenant in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following: i.    That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and Public Works prior to the issuance of a building permit: 1.    Full frontage improvements; 2.    A storm water management plan; and ii.    That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and Public Works prior to any land alteration: 1.    A construction parking management plan; and 2.    A mitigation plan. iii.    That the properties be consolidated prior to issuance of a Development Permit for Form and Character; iv.    That prior to issuance of a building permit, an access easement through the site to lands beyond be registered, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer; v.    That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the proposed development that ensures residential parking is allocated to each unit and visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in exchange for compensation separate from that of a residential unit; vi.    That the building be constructed with electric heat pumps for each individual unit or a central electric heat pump system; vii.    That tree protection measures, inclusive of tree protection fencing, are implemented prior to commencement of work to protect the two trees in the southwest corner that have been identified for retention; viii.    That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets or exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type III Environmental Product Declaration that is 3rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming Potential value and confirming that the proposed development meets the requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN; ix.     That the drawings submitted for approval as part of the Development Permit application substantially comply with what has been presented to Council through this rezoning application (Z26-0004).

canonical_motions.source_motion_text: THAT Temporary Use Permit No. TUP26-0004 is issued by the Council for the City of Langford to Honeycomb Cannabis Inc to operate a non-medical cannabis retail store on the property legally described as Parcel 1, Plan VIP81886, Section 1, Range 3W, Highland District, (Being a Consolidation of Lot A & B see CA3468036), PID No. 029-213-533 (107-2317 Millstream Road), in accordance with Section 493 of the Local Government Act , subject to the following terms and conditions, and notwithstanding Sec. 3.02.02(5) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300: 1. Conditions a) Exterior walls shall be treated in a manner and colour that is consistent with other parts of the building which the business occupies. If the non-medical cannabis retail store occupies a standalone building, then the exterior of the building will exhibit colours from a muted, earth tone palette with contrasting accent colours for windows, trim and doors. Bold or vivid colours that are intended to be distinctive and eye-catching (e.g.: lime green or fire engine red) may be used on signage, but not on the building façade or trim to the satisfaction of the Director of Community Planning and Development Services; b) All windows shall be opaque or constructed with spandrel panels behind. Windows and spandrels may not be embellished with any form of imagery; c) Security devices, such as window bars or roll shutters, shall be deployed on the inside of doors or windows so as to be unobtrusive and invisible from the street; d) The applicant shall provide security measures associated with the premises from which the nonmedical cannabis retail store will operate in accordance with the applicant’s proposal in response to the City of Langford Request for Proposal for the Retail Sales of Cannabis and Cannabis Related Products (RFP), as determined by the Chief Administrative Officer; e) The applicant shall address issues of nuisance with respect to odours, smoke and noise relating to public use of cannabis and cannabis products in accordance with the applicant’s proposal in response to the RFP and the regulations, terms and conditions outlined in the Cannabis Control and Licencing Act of B.C.; f) The applicant shall address impairment issues relating to public use of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medical purposes in accordance with the applicant’s proposal in response to the RFP and the regulations, terms and conditions outlined in the Cannabis Control and Licencing Act of B.C .; g) The non-medical cannabis retail store must be a stand-alone business; h) The hours of operation of the non-medical cannabis retail store shall be limited to 9am to 9pm Sunday through Wednesday and 9am to 10pm Thursday through Saturday; i) The applicant shall provide educational initiatives and materials associated with the impacts and related social concerns of the non-medical use of cannabis and cannabis products in accordance with the applicant’s proposal in response to the RFP and as outlined in the Cannabis Retail Store Terms and Conditions, a handbook for the sale of non-medical cannabis in British Columbia ; j) The applicant shall conform to the regulations stipulated in the Cannabis Control and Licencing Act of British Columbia B.C. Reg.202/2018 ; k) The Applicant shall ensure that the non-medical cannabis retail sale is in compliance with all applicable laws, including all City bylaws; SIGNAGE l) All signage shall be subject to a subsequent Sign Development Permit application process and shall be constructed and placed in accordance with Langford Sign Bylaw No.1250 and to the satisfaction of the Director of Community Planning and Development Services; m) All signage shall be architecturally compatible with the style, composition, materials, colours, and details of the buildings within the development; n) The location and size of signs shall be architecturally integrated with the overall design of the buildings; o) As a condition of issuance of this permit, and notwithstanding what is permitted by Bylaw No. 1250, the business is limited to three signs only . This signage shall indicate the name of the business only, and shall not display company slogans, and may not employ any play on words with respect to cannabis or drug culture. This signage may be internally illuminated in accordance with City guidelines, but may not be animated in any way or have variable messaging; p) Notwithstanding article o), the business may have one illuminated sign which indicates that the business is open, provided that this signage is affixed to the interior of a door or window visible from the street and does not exceed an area of 0.2m2 (2ft2); q) Sandwich board type signs are prohibited; If a previous Development Permit has been issued with respect to Form and Character and no new buildings or exterior renovations are being proposed some of these conditions may be waived. 2. Whereas a) The non-medicinal use of cannabis and cannabis related products has historically been prohibited by federal law in Canada and, as a result, has historically been prohibited by the City under its Zoning Bylaw No. 300; b) On October 17, 2018, the Federal Government legalized the non-medicinal use of cannabis and cannabis products; c) The Federal Government and the Provincial Government have developed a regulatory framework for the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medicinal use; d) The City wishes to authorize the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products within its boundaries, but recognizes that there are challenges associated with it doing so; e) The City issued the Request for Proposals for the Retail Sales of Cannabis and Cannabis Related Products to seek proposals from individuals and organizations interested in undertaking the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medicinal use within the City’s boundaries, and required that proposals include details as to how the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products would be addressed; f) The City received and reviewed over 30 proposals in response to the Request for Proposals, and identified Honeycomb Cannabis Inc. proposal as one that best addressed the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products; and, g) Honeycomb Cannabis Inc. is committed to assisting the City and taking positive steps to address the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products; Now therefore be it resolved that Council issue Temporary Use Permit TUP26-0004 to Honeycomb Cannabis Inc for it to operate a Cannabis Retail Store at 107-2317 Millstream Road for a three-year term subject to the terms and conditions listed within. 3. Expiry THAT the Temporary Use Permit be issued for a period of 36 months and will expire on September 8, 2029. Authorized Resolution passed by the Council of the City of Langford on September 8, 2026. Permit issued on September 8, 2026.

Reg.202/2018 ; k) The Applicant shall ensure that the non-medical cannabis retail sale is in compliance with all applicable laws, including all City bylaws; SIGNAGE l) All signage shall be subject to a subsequent Sign Development Permit application process and shall be constructed and placed in accordance with Langford Sign Bylaw No.1250 and to the satisfaction of the Director of Community Planning and Development Services; m) All signage shall be architecturally compatible with the style, composition, materials, colours, and details of the buildings within the development; n) The location and size of signs shall be architecturally integrated with the overall design of the buildings; o) As a condition of issuance of this permit, and notwithstanding what is permitted by Bylaw No. 1250, the business is limited to three signs only . This signage shall indicate the name of the business only, and shall not display company slogans, and may not employ any play on words with respect to cannabis or drug culture. This signage may be internally illuminated in accordance with City guidelines, but may not be animated in any way or have variable messaging; p) Notwithstanding article o), the business may have one illuminated sign which indicates that the business is open, provided that this signage is affixed to the interior of a door or window visible from the street and does not exceed an area of 0.2m2 (2ft2); q) Sandwich board type signs are prohibited; If a previous Development Permit has been issued with respect to Form and Character and no new buildings or exterior renovations are being proposed some of these conditions may be waived. 2. Whereas a) The non-medicinal use of cannabis and cannabis related products has historically been prohibited by federal law in Canada and, as a result, has historically been prohibited by the City under its Zoning Bylaw No. 300; b) On October 17, 2018, the Federal Government legalized the non-medicinal use of cannabis and cannabis products; c) The Federal Government and the Provincial Government have developed a regulatory framework for the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medicinal use; d) The City wishes to authorize the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products within its boundaries, but recognizes that there are challenges associated with it doing so; e) The City issued the Request for Proposals for the Retail Sales of Cannabis and Cannabis Related Products to seek proposals from individuals and organizations interested in undertaking the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products for non-medicinal use within the City’s boundaries, and required that proposals include details as to how the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products would be addressed; f) The City received and reviewed over 30 proposals in response to the Request for Proposals, and identified Honeycomb Cannabis Inc. proposal as one that best addressed the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products; and, g) Honeycomb Cannabis Inc. is committed to assisting the City and taking positive steps to address the challenges with the retail sale of cannabis and cannabis products; Now therefore be it resolved that Council issue Temporary Use Permit TUP26-0004 to Honeycomb Cannabis Inc for it to operate a Cannabis Retail Store at 107-2317 Millstream Road for a three-year term subject to the terms and conditions listed within. 3. Expiry THAT the Temporary Use Permit be issued for a period of 36 months and will expire on September 8, 2029. Authorized Resolution passed by the Council of the City of Langford on September 8, 2026. Permit issued on September 8, 2026.
Motion  CARRIED.

canonical_motions.after_outcome: 12.2.3 Bylaw No. 2236 – Application to Rezone 709, 711, 715, 719, and 721 Massie Drive

canonical_motions.agenda_item_title: Bylaw No. 2236 – Application to Rezone 709, 711, 715, 719, and 721 Massie Drive
canonical_motions.source_motion_text: THAT Council: Consider bringing forward Bylaw No. 2236 for 1 st , 2 nd , and 3 rd readings at a future Council meeting in order to amend the zoning designation of the properties located at 709/711, 715, 719, and 721 Massie Drive from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) Zone to the Medium Density Residential (RM6) Zone subject to the following terms and conditions: That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption , registers a Section 219 covenant in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following: That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a building permit: Full frontage improvements; and A storm water management plan. That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to any land alteration: A construction parking management plan; and A mitigation plan. That the properties be consolidated prior to issuance of a Development Permit for Form and Character; That prior to the issuance of a Building Permit, the following contributions are provided: $2,850 per residential unit created towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund on the 1st through 4th storeys; $1,425 per residential unit created towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund on the 5th and 6th storeys; $750 per unit created towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund on the 1st through 4th storeys; and $375 per unit created towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund on the 5th and 6th storeys. That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the proposed development that ensures that any residential parking is not provided in exchange for compensation separate from that of a residential unit; That the building constructed on the properties include a minimum of ten dwelling units designed and built as 3-bedroom units; That tree protection measures, inclusive of tree protection fencing, are implemented prior to commencement of work to protect the trees identified for retention in the arborist report throughout the construction period, as per the arborist report prepared by Talmack Urban Forestry, dated July 10, 2025; That all concrete used on-site will utilize ready-mix concrete that meets or exceeds the weighted average Global Warming Potential targets based on Concrete BC Baseline (average) mix data, and that prior to the issuance of a Building Permit the applicant shall provide a Type III Environmental Product Declaration that is 3 rd party verified specifying the total Global Warming Potential value and confirming that the proposed development meets the requirements of Low Carbon Concrete Policy POL-0167-PLAN; That, prior to the issuance of a Building Permit, the developer enters into a Housing Agreement with the City that requires a minimum 10% of units constructed be rented for at least 10% below the benchmark rent for the unit type for a term not less than 25 years or that a minimum of 5% of units constructed be directed to and sold in accordance with the terms of the Attainable Home Ownership Program Policy (POL-0166-PLAN). The developer shall identify the Attainable Units on the plans submitted for the required Development Permit application, and ensure at least 50% of the required attainable housing units have two or more bedrooms; and That the building be constructed with electric heat pumps.

16. NOTICE OF MOTION
16.1 Advocacy for the BC Ministry of Education and Childcare to reinstate funding to the ARC Foundation
Councillor Guiry read aloud the following Notice of Motion for consideration at the next regularly scheduled Council meeting: "WHEREAS, the ARC Foundation developed SOGI 123 in collaboration with the B.C. Ministry of Education, B.C. Teachers' Federation, The University of British Columbia's faculty of education, Out in Schools, nine school districts throughout B.C., and local, national and international LGBTQ community organizations and SOGI 123 has been used in BC schools since 2016; AND WHEREAS, the ARC Foundation works with school districts to provide SOGI 123 resources which are a set of tools that teachers can use to ensure their classrooms are accepting and rooted in respect and belonging; AND WHEREAS, the ARC Foundation has had to address a significant funding gap by reducing staffing levels as of July 2026 due to the recent discontinuation of funding by the BC Ministry of Education and Childcare; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the City of Langford Mayor and Council to direct staff to write a letter to the Minister of Education and Childcare and MLA Ravi Parmar, asking that the ministry reinstate funding to the ARC Foundation and affirm the importance of the SOGI 123 program so that school districts will continue to work with the ARC Foundation to access resources to create a safe and inclusive environment for all students, regardless of their sexual orientation or gender identity, or the diversity in their own families."
